body:
# My 13 Favorite Things to Do in Tampa (From Riverwalk to Ybor)

I went in expecting one tidy list of things to do in Tampa. What I found was a city that works more like a handful of neighborhoods, each with its own personality and its own logistics. 🌴

There's a walkable downtown clump of waterfront attractions, a pair of big theme parks to the north, a zoo and an old Cuban-and-Italian cigar district. The main challenge is that these places are spread out, and a couple of them have confusing addresses. Busch Gardens and Adventure Island are the classic example.

Based on everything I explored, here are my favorite things to do in Tampa FL, plus the practical tips I wish I'd had before I arrived. Along the way I've included free activities, options for adults and a few places worth a trip just outside the city.

![Walkers on the Tampa Riverwalk beside the Hillsborough River near Curtis Hixon Park](https://images.pexels.com/photos/20739680/pexels-photo-20739680.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Nate Biddle](https://www.pexels.com/@nxbid0) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/cyclist-20739680/)*

## Short on Time? Here Are My Quick Travel Tips ⏱️

This is a detailed guide, so if you just want the essentials, start here.

- **My top Tampa recommendations:** These are my picks for the best things to do in Tampa.
  - Walk the Riverwalk, because it ties the best downtown stuff together.
  - Visit ZooTampa for the manatees.
  - Spend an evening on Seventh Avenue in Ybor City for a completely different feel from the rest of town.
- **If you want to save money:** The TECO Line streetcar is free seven days a week, and walking the Riverwalk costs nothing. If you plan to see several attractions, look into the Riverwalk Attraction Pass, and check exactly which attractions are included and what it costs when you buy.
- **Where to start:** Heights Market at Armature Works, 1910 N Ola Avenue, is the easiest launch point for the Riverwalk.
- **Getting around:** Stay on foot and on the streetcar downtown, and drive to the zoo and the theme parks.
- **One thing I learned the hard way:** Don't treat Busch Gardens and Adventure Island as one address. They have separate street addresses and share one phone number.

## Getting Around Tampa

Tampa is easier once you plan by area. Most Tampa Florida things to do fall into three groups: downtown on foot, the north-side parks by car, and Ybor City, which you can reach by streetcar. Sorting the things to do Tampa Florida offers into those groups saved me a lot of backtracking.

### Downtown on Foot and by Streetcar

The Riverwalk, the aquarium, the museums, the parks and the arena sit close together. I'd leave the car parked and walk. Parking rates can change, so check them at the entrance before you commit.

The TECO Line streetcar covers the rest. It runs 2.7 miles from downtown through the Channel District to Ybor City, with 11 stations, and it's free. Trains come about every 15 to 20 minutes, so check the schedule before you count on it.

### Driving to the North-Side Parks

ZooTampa, Busch Gardens and Adventure Island are all north of downtown, so you'll want a car or a ride. Each has its own address in the sections below. Put the exact street address into your GPS rather than just the park name.

### On the Water

Tampa looks different from the water. I've covered the boat options in item 7.

## 1. Walk the Tampa Riverwalk

![Riverwalk path along the Hillsborough River in downtown Tampa](https://images.pexels.com/photos/36029477/pexels-photo-36029477.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Mark Stebnicki](https://www.pexels.com/@nc-farm-bureau-mark) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-wilmington-riverfront-skyline-36029477/)*

If I could only recommend one thing, this would be it. The Riverwalk is 2.6 miles from the Hillsborough River to the Garrison Channel, and it links many of the downtown places in this guide. You can walk it, bike it or take a scooter.

I'd start at the north end at Heights Market in Armature Works, then follow the path through Curtis Hixon Park and on to Sparkman Wharf. You pass parks, museums and waterfront views, and you can stop whenever your feet need a break. It's the best way I found to understand how downtown fits together.

**Tip:** Do the whole route in sections if it's hot. The food stops at each end make good breaks.

**Address:** Heights Market, Armature Works, 1910 N Ola Avenue, Tampa (north end of the walk).

## 2. Meet the Sea Creatures at The Florida Aquarium

![Otters at The Florida Aquarium in the Channel District, Tampa](https://images.pexels.com/photos/13866083/pexels-photo-13866083.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Tibor Szabo](https://www.pexels.com/@tibszabo) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/close-up-photograph-of-otters-13866083/)*

This is one of the great things to do in Tampa when the weather isn't cooperating, and it's also an easy pick if you're traveling with kids. The aquarium has thousands of animals, including otters and lemurs. You can also add a Bay Spirit II dolphin trip.

I liked how central it is. It sits between two cruise terminals, right on the streetcar line, so you can reach it without a car. It also works as a pre-cruise stop.

**Tip:** Check the opening hours the morning you go, because they can change. The aquarium also runs a Guppyween event later in October, so check the dates if you're visiting then.

**Address:** 701 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602. Phone: (813) 273-4000.

**How to Get There:** Take the TECO Line streetcar to the Channel District. The aquarium is between two cruise terminals.

## 3. Ride the Free TECO Line Streetcar

![TECO Line streetcar stopped in downtown Tampa](https://images.pexels.com/photos/12350835/pexels-photo-12350835.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Eyes2Soul Eyes2Soul](https://www.pexels.com/@eyes2soul) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/modern-city-tram-on-stop-12350835/)*

Free things to do in Tampa are not easy to come by, so I'm giving the streetcar its own spot. It's transport and sightseeing in one. The line runs 2.7 miles through downtown and the Channel District to Ybor City, free seven days a week, with 11 stations. 🚋

I used it to link the waterfront with Ybor without worrying about parking at both ends. You'll wait about 15 to 20 minutes between trains, so it's not a "dash for it" kind of system. Just build in a little slack.

**Tip:** Ride it one way toward Ybor in the afternoon, and plan to stay for dinner on Seventh Avenue.

**How to Get There:** Look for the stations in downtown, the Channel District and Ybor City. Check the schedule before you go.

## 4. Explore the Museums on Water Street and Gasparilla Plaza

![Tampa Bay History Center and the museums near Gasparilla Plaza in downtown Tampa](https://images.pexels.com/photos/35120562/pexels-photo-35120562.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Stephen Leonardi](https://www.pexels.com/@stephen-leonardi-587681991) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/uss-midway-museum-at-night-in-san-diego-35120562/)*

Three museums sit close together downtown, so you can mix and match depending on your group.

- **Tampa Bay History Center:** 12,000 years of local history, including the Treasure Seekers exhibit. It's at 801 Water Street.
- **Tampa Museum of Art:** 120 W Gasparilla Plaza.
- **Glazer Children's Museum:** 110 West Gasparilla Plaza. It's best for kids under 12, so I'd skip it if you're traveling without them.

**Tip:** Don't expect museum admission to be free. Check ticket prices before you go. If you're planning to see several attractions, the Riverwalk Attraction Pass may be worth a look. Confirm which places it includes.

## 5. Relax in Curtis Hixon and the Riverfront Parks

![Curtis Hixon Park on the Tampa riverfront](https://images.pexels.com/photos/38197218/pexels-photo-38197218.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Roy Serafin](https://www.pexels.com/@roythephotographer) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/scenic-view-of-historic-st-augustine-waterfront-38197218/)*

Among all the Tampa FL things to do, a lazy afternoon in a park is easy to overlook. It shouldn't be. Curtis Hixon Park is about 8 acres, sits right on the Riverwalk and has yoga on Sundays.

A few more parks are worth knowing about:

- **Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park:** about 25 acres, north of the University of Tampa and across from the Straz.
- **Water Works Park:** 1701 N Highland Avenue.
- **Cotanchobee Park:** another riverfront park along the water.

**Tip:** If you want yoga, check the schedule before you go, since classes can change.

**Address:** Curtis Hixon Park, 600 N Ashley Drive, Tampa. Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park, 1001 North Boulevard, Tampa.

## 6. Eat and Wander at Armature Works, Sparkman Wharf and Ulele

![Armature Works food hall in the former trolley barn in Tampa](https://images.pexels.com/photos/37100502/pexels-photo-37100502.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [James Mirakian](https://www.pexels.com/@james-mirakian-774977502) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/bustling-interior-of-west-side-market-cleveland-37100502/)*

The two ends of the Riverwalk are also good places to eat and hang out. Armature Works, the old trolley barn, is now a food hall and the start of the walk. Sparkman Wharf sits at the other end, close to the arena, so it works well before or after a Lightning game.

Ulele, at 1810 N Highland Avenue, is another well-known Riverwalk stop. It debuted in 2014. I'd pick based on your appetite and your timing.

**Tip:** Check opening hours, since they vary by spot.

**Address:** Armature Works, 1910 N Ola Avenue. Sparkman Wharf, 615 Channelside Drive. Ulele, 1810 N Highland Avenue. All in Tampa.

## 7. Get Out on the Water

![Water taxi on the Hillsborough River in downtown Tampa](https://images.pexels.com/photos/30554305/pexels-photo-30554305.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [AJ  Ahamad](https://www.pexels.com/@aj-ahamad-767001191) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-water-taxi-on-dubai-s-scenic-waters-30554305/)*

You have plenty of ways to see Tampa from the water, including eBoats, Pirate Water Taxi, Riverwalk Boating, Tampa Bay Fun Boat, Tampa Bay Waterbike and Yacht Starship. Sail Plaza and the water taxi both use 333 South Franklin as their address.

If you like ships, the American Victory is at 705 Channelside. It was delivered May 24, 1945, and is billed as one of three fully functioning ships of its kind.

**Tip:** Boat schedules and prices vary by operator, so check before you head out.

**Address:** Sail Plaza and the water taxi, 333 South Franklin, Tampa. American Victory, 705 Channelside, Tampa.

## 8. Catch a Show at the Straz Center

![Exterior of the Straz Center for the Performing Arts in downtown Tampa](https://images.pexels.com/photos/13257233/pexels-photo-13257233.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Laura Paredis](https://www.pexels.com/@laura-paredis-1047081) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/the-roofing-of-the-kilden-performing-arts-centre-13257233/)*

One of the coolest things to do in Tampa after dark is catch a performance at the Straz. It's a big theater complex with Broadway shows, the Florida Orchestra and Opera Tampa.

It's right across from Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park, so you can walk the riverfront before curtain.

**Tip:** Check what's on and book ahead for the show you want.

**Address:** 1010 North Macinnes Place, Tampa.

## 9. Go to a Lightning Game or Event at Benchmark International Arena

![Benchmark International Arena on Channelside Drive in Tampa](https://images.pexels.com/photos/13237897/pexels-photo-13237897.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Scott Foltz](https://www.pexels.com/@scottyfoltz95) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/fast-moving-car-on-a-race-track-13237897/)*

This is the home of the Lightning, and it hosts well over 150 events a year. It sits between The Florida Aquarium and the convention center, so it's an easy add to a downtown day.

**Tip:** Some places still call it Amalie Arena. Match the address, 401 Channelside Drive, rather than the old name.

**Address:** 401 Channelside Drive, Tampa.

## 10. Meet the Manatees at ZooTampa at Lowry Park

![Manatee at ZooTampa at Lowry Park](https://images.pexels.com/photos/12237825/pexels-photo-12237825.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Jorge Luis Morales](https://www.pexels.com/@jorge-luis-morales-238540862) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/close-up-photo-of-sea-lion-underwater-12237825/)*

For fun things to do in Tampa, this is my top family pick, and it's one of the things I'd tell any first-timer to see. The zoo has around 2,000 animals, including Florida panthers, an Africa area and a Florida Waters section with manatees, jellies and otters. The manatee hospital has been running since 1991.

**Tip:** Check hours the morning you go. The zoo also runs Creatures of the Night on select October nights, so check dates and whether that needs a separate ticket.

**Address:** 1101 W. Sligh Avenue, Tampa, FL 33604. Phone: (813) 935-8552.

**How to Get There:** Drive or take a ride to the address above.

## 11. Ride the Coasters at Busch Gardens

![Roller coaster at Busch Gardens Tampa Bay](https://images.pexels.com/photos/38331893/pexels-photo-38331893.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [marclyc li](https://www.pexels.com/@marclyc-li-2160558161) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/colorful-amusement-park-ride-with-sculpture-38331893/)*

Busch Gardens calls itself the coaster capital of Florida, and it has 200-plus species of animals too. Iron Gwazi and Cheetah Hunt are the names I'd look for, and Falcon's Fury stands 335 feet tall. Tigris is one of the newer rides. 🎢

Getting there is simple once you know the layout. The park is about eight miles northeast of downtown, two miles east of I-275 at Busch Boulevard, and two miles west of I-75 exit 265. It's about an hour from Orlando on I-4 and roughly 30 minutes east of the beaches and the airport.

**Tip:** Spooktacular runs on Saturdays and Sundays from September 12 through November 1. A separate after-dark event needs its own ticket, so check before you buy.

**Address:** 10165 N McKinley Drive, Tampa, FL 33612. That address does not take mail.

## 12. Splash Around at Adventure Island

![Water slides at Adventure Island in Tampa](https://images.pexels.com/photos/31166924/pexels-photo-31166924.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Vika Glitter](https://www.pexels.com/@vika-glitter-392079) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/thrilling-water-slide-adventure-with-inner-tube-31166924/)*

Adventure Island is the water park next door, and it's one of the best fun things to do Tampa has for a hot day. It covers about 30 acres and has a slide called Colossal Curl.

Here's where I'd be careful. The park's own directions put it north of Busch Gardens, so follow those rather than looking for it right across the street.

**Tip:** Busch Gardens and Adventure Island share one phone number, (813) 884-4386, which is how people end up calling the wrong gate. Double-check which park you need.

**Address:** 10001 N McKinley Drive, Tampa, FL 33612.

## 13. Step Back in Time in Ybor City

![Seventh Avenue in the Ybor City Historic District, Tampa](https://images.pexels.com/photos/4250339/pexels-photo-4250339.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Brett Sayles](https://www.pexels.com/@brett-sayles) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/urban-street-with-illuminating-lights-at-night-4250339/)*

Among all the things to do in Tampa Florida, Ybor City is the one that feels least like a theme park or a riverwalk. It's a National Historic Landmark northeast of downtown, with more than 950 buildings. Visit Seventh Avenue, nicknamed La Sétima, which runs from Nick Nuccio Parkway for 11 blocks to 26th Street.

Look for the Columbia, the Italian Club, El Centro Español and the Ritz. The district dates to 1885.

**Tip:** Ride the free streetcar to get here. Since Seventh Avenue is a lively nightlife street after dark, plan your ride home.

**How to Get There:** Take the TECO Line streetcar to Ybor City.

## Free Things to Do in Tampa

The free things to do Tampa offers are few, but they're good. If you're after free things to do in Tampa Florida, here are the ones I can vouch for:

- **Ride the TECO Line streetcar.** It's free seven days a week.
- **Walk the Riverwalk.** There's no ticket for the walk itself.

Museums, the aquarium, the zoo and the theme parks all charge admission, so check prices before you go. For things to do in Tampa for free, the streetcar plus the Riverwalk makes a solid day.

## Things to Do Near Tampa FL

If you have extra time, some good places sit just outside the city. Lettuce Lake Park in north Tampa and Hillsborough River State Park in Thonotosassa are the nearby nature options.

For beaches, head to Clearwater, St. Pete Beach and Caladesi. These are all things to do near Tampa that make a good day trip from the city.

## Cool Things to Do in Tampa Florida for Adults

For adults, I'd lean toward the Straz, Lightning games and the after-dark park nights, which are separately ticketed. The Glazer Children's Museum is aimed at kids, so I'd skip it without them.

## Visiting Tampa in October: Weekend and Saturday Options

October is a good time for seasonal events. Busch Gardens runs Spooktacular on Saturdays and Sundays from September 12 through November 1, plus a separately ticketed after-dark event. ZooTampa has Creatures of the Night on select October nights. The aquarium has Guppyween later in the month.

Dates and tickets can change, so check each park before you plan your weekend. 🌅

## Useful Things to Know Before You Go

- **Check today's hours before you go.** Opening hours can change, so look them up the morning of your visit. I wouldn't plan a whole week around a single notice.
- **Match the address, not the old name.** The arena is Benchmark International Arena at 401 Channelside Drive, though some guides still say Amalie Arena.
- **Busch Gardens and Adventure Island have two addresses.** Busch Gardens is at 10165 N McKinley Drive and Adventure Island is at 10001 N McKinley Drive. They share one phone number, so if you're going to both, save both addresses.
- **Confirm the pass before you buy.** Check exactly which attractions the Riverwalk Attraction Pass includes, and what it costs.
- **Night events are separate.** Seasonal after-dark events may need a separate ticket.
- **Plan by area.** Group downtown stops, north-side parks and Ybor City into separate days or half-days.

## FAQ

### What are the best things to do in Tampa Florida?

I'd start with the Riverwalk, The Florida Aquarium, ZooTampa, Busch Gardens and Ybor City. They cover downtown, the north-side parks and the historic district.

### What are fun things to do in Tampa Florida?

The zoo, the aquarium and the theme parks are the most fun for families. Adventure Island is the pick on a hot day.

### Are there free things to do in Tampa Florida?

Yes. The TECO Line streetcar is free seven days a week, and walking the Riverwalk costs nothing.

### What are the things to do near Tampa FL?

Lettuce Lake Park and Hillsborough River State Park are close, and the beaches at Clearwater, St. Pete Beach and Caladesi are a short trip away.

### What is there to do in Tampa this weekend or on a Saturday?

Busch Gardens runs Spooktacular on Saturdays and Sundays through November 1. ZooTampa has select October nights. Check the dates before you go.

### Are Busch Gardens and Adventure Island at the same address?

No. Busch Gardens is at 10165 N McKinley Drive and Adventure Island is at 10001 N McKinley Drive. They share one phone number.

### How do I get between downtown and Ybor City?

Take the free TECO Line streetcar. It runs 2.7 miles with 11 stations.

### How long is the Tampa Riverwalk?

The Riverwalk is 2.6 miles, from the Hillsborough River to the Garrison Channel.

## Final Thoughts

Tampa won me over because it isn't one thing. You can spend a morning on the Riverwalk, an afternoon with manatees and an evening on Seventh Avenue, and it feels like three different trips. That's what makes the things to do in Tampa so rewarding.

My big planning tip is to organize your days by area. Keep downtown on foot, give the north-side parks their own day, and save Ybor City for the evening. That's the best way I found to enjoy the Tampa things to do on this list without wasting time in the car.

body:
# Ulele, Tampa: My Honest Guide (What to Know Before You Go)

I walked up to Ulele Tampa expecting a pretty riverside dinner spot and not much more. I also said the name wrong the whole way there. It's pronounced You-lay-lee, and the restaurant set me straight. 😄

Ulele is a native-inspired lunch and dinner restaurant on Tampa's Riverwalk, inside a reimagined 1903 water works building in Tampa Heights. The food comes off a huge barbacoa grill, and the beer is brewed on site. The challenges are small but real: getting a table, getting the dress code right and not mixing it up with another Ulele.

Here is everything I'd want a friend to tell me before going, from reservations and parking to what to drink and what to skip.

![Exterior of Ulele restaurant in the historic Water Works building on the Hillsborough River in Tampa Heights](https://images.pexels.com/photos/10895022/pexels-photo-10895022.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Vitaly Kushnir](https://www.pexels.com/@kartatos) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/grayscale-photography-of-a-building-near-pond-10895022/)*

## Short on Time? Here Are My Quick Travel Tips ⚡

This is a detailed guide, so if you just want the essentials, start here.

**My top recommendations:**

- **Call ahead for a table.** The patio and waterfront seats are the ones everyone wants at sunset.
- **Try the house-brewed beer.** It's made on site, and you can only get it at Ulele.
- **Walk Water Works Park next door.** It's the easiest way to burn off a heavy plate or kill time before your table is ready.

**Where to start:** The Riverwalk. Plenty of downtown hotel guests walk to Ulele along the river.

**Where to park:** Plan on valet at the front drive when it's running. Street parking fills up fast on busy nights.

**One thing I'd double-check before leaving the hotel:** Men need sleeves for the main dining rooms. Otherwise you may get steered to the patio.

## What It's Like

Ulele sits at 1810 North Highland Avenue in Tampa Heights, right on the Hillsborough River. It's about 400 yards from the Straz Center for the Performing Arts. It opened in August 2014 and is part of the Columbia Restaurant Group. It shares a family tree with other Columbia restaurants, including the one in Ybor City, but it's a completely different concept.

![Dining room and riverside patio at Ulele with the Hillsborough River in the background](https://images.pexels.com/photos/8753757/pexels-photo-8753757.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Team Picsfast](https://www.pexels.com/@picsfast) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/fresh-pizza-and-beer-on-railing-of-balcony-8753757/)*

The restaurant calls its food native-inspired. The story it tells is about Florida's waters and land, with ingredients that would have been familiar to the Native peoples of the area, including the princess the restaurant is named for. There are multicultural and European-explorer threads too. The sourcing philosophy is simple: Florida produce and seafood when available, U.S. family farms otherwise, and organic where they can. In that organic line, there are no hormones or antibiotics.

The star of the kitchen is a 10-foot-diameter barbacoa grill. Dishes come off it, and it's the heart of the place.

The building itself is the reason I'd come even if the food were average. It's the old Tampa Heights Water Works building, sitting beside Ulele Spring and next to Water Works Park. You feel the history as you walk in.

It's a big restaurant, too. There's nearly 7,000 square feet, with about 240 seats inside, about 95 in the beer garden and about 50 on the rooftop terrace with river views. The lawn can handle private events of about 400 people.

The riverside seats are the draw, and they're also the ones that bake in the afternoon sun before the river breeze kicks in. In summer, I'd save those tables for later in the day.

## What to Order

I'm not going to invent an entree list for you, because the menu changes. Ask for the current one when you sit down. What I can tell you is what I'd build the meal around.

![Barbacoa grill at Ulele restaurant with food cooking over the flames](https://images.pexels.com/photos/5779781/pexels-photo-5779781.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [RDNE Stock project](https://www.pexels.com/@rdne) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-person-cooking-on-the-grill-5779781/)*

**Anything off the barbacoa grill.** The 10-foot grill is the whole point of the kitchen, so I'd choose from the dishes that come off it. After a heavy plate, I was very glad Water Works Park was next door for a walk.

**The house-brewed beer.** The on-site brewery is Ulele Spring Brewery, and the regular tank-to-tap lineup includes:

- Rusty Red
- Water Works Pale
- Hydration Station Lager
- Ulele Light
- Magbee's Honey Lager
- Wedding Beer

There are seasonal beers too. You won't find these anywhere else, since the craft beer is only available at Ulele and made right there.

**Wine, if you prefer it.** The list leans on domestic family-winery wines, plus some Spanish private-label bottles as a nod to the early Spanish explorers.

**A to-go drink for the Riverwalk.** Beer and cocktails can be ordered to go in a special cup that lets you drink legally along the 2.4-mile Tampa Riverwalk. That's a very Tampa quirk. Stay within the Riverwalk rules, and don't wander into traffic with a drink.

## Hours and Reservations

![Host stand and waiting guests at the entrance of Ulele in Tampa Heights](https://images.pexels.com/photos/8312018/pexels-photo-8312018.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Denys Gromov](https://www.pexels.com/@jdgromov) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/ukulele-and-picture-frames-on-a-blue-wall-8312018/)*

Ulele serves lunch and dinner daily:

| Days | Hours |
| --- | --- |
| Sunday–Thursday | 11 a.m.–10 p.m. |
| Friday and Saturday | 11 a.m.–11 p.m. |

The restaurant is closed on Thanksgiving and Christmas. Hours can change, so check them the morning you go.

The kitchen opens at 11 a.m. and the restaurant serves lunch and dinner, so don't show up at 9:30 a.m. hoping for eggs.

Reservations are the first struggle. Call **813-999-4952** to book. If you hit a recording, leave the details you want. You can also book through OpenTable, but online booking didn't go through for me, and the phone was what worked. Parties of 7 or more should call instead of relying on a quick online booking. Groups of 20 or more should contact **813-310-3701** or **groups@Ulele.com**. For general questions, the email is **info@ulele.com**.

Don't treat reservations as optional on a nice evening. On a clear Saturday, I watched walk-ups lingering by the host stand while reserved parties flowed past them to the river side. If you have tickets at the Straz, build in walking time. A 5:30 curtain doesn't mean you can count on a same-day riverside table for four without calling first.

## Parking and Getting There

**Address:** 1810 North Highland Avenue, Tampa, FL 33602
**Phone:** 813-999-4952

![Front drive and entrance of Ulele on North Highland Avenue in Tampa Heights](https://images.pexels.com/photos/36756673/pexels-photo-36756673.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Matt Fitz Gibaud](https://www.pexels.com/@mfitzart) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/charming-street-view-with-boutique-and-palm-tree-36756673/)*

Parking is where people get tense before they ever taste the food. Here's how I'd plan it.

### Driving and Valet

The restaurant fronts Highland Avenue. When Ulele opened, complimentary valet at the front drive was part of the plan for Columbia Restaurant Group properties. Ask at the entrance whether it's running when you arrive, and check for any current charge.

Street parking near the building fills around curtain times at the Straz and during weekend brunch hours. I wouldn't bet a reservation on finding a free curb spot at 6:45 p.m. on a Saturday.

### Walking the Riverwalk

The Riverwalk is the approach a lot of downtown hotel guests take, and it's a pretty one. You can also walk in from the Water Works Park or Doyle Carlton side. Leave extra time in summer heat. It's a lovely walk, but you'll arrive warm.

### Bike, Boat, Canoe or Kayak

You can also arrive by bike or on foot. If you're on the water, you can come by boat, canoe or kayak and dock next door at Water Works Park. I didn't arrive this way, but it's the most memorable way to get there.

## Tips Before You Go

**Say the name with confidence.** It's You-lay-lee. Softening the vowels at the host stand is a common mistake, and nobody minds, but it's nice to get it right.

**Wear sleeves if you want the indoor rooms.** The atmosphere is casual elegance. Formal is fine and up to you, but men must wear sleeves. If you're dressed more relaxed than they want for the main dining rooms, you may be seated outdoors instead. I watched a host redirect a sleeveless guest toward the patio. That surprises beach-vacation visitors who walked the Riverwalk in tank tops.

**Know which Ulele you mean.** There's a second Ulele at Tampa International Airport in Airside C, near Southwest. If your layover is the only meal you have, that's the one for you. If you want the brewery, the barbacoa grill, the rooftop and Water Works Park next door, you want the Tampa Heights restaurant on Highland Avenue.

**Don't mix it up with Columbia.** Whether you search Tampa Ulele, ulele restaurant tampa or ulele restaurant tampa florida, you're looking for one riverside dining room on Highland Avenue. It isn't the Columbia Cafe at the History Center or the Columbia in Ybor City. They're the same company, but separate restaurants in different places.

**Ask for the current menu.** The offerings change, so I'm not quoting prices. Ask what's on offer when you sit down, and check the seasonal beers.

**Make a plan for the walk.** Water Works Park is great for families and for anyone who needs to move after dinner. I'd arrive early enough to stroll before or after the meal.

## Ulele Tampa FAQ

### How do you pronounce Ulele?

It's pronounced You-lay-lee. The spelling doesn't give it away, so don't feel bad if you get it wrong at first.

### Where is Ulele in Tampa?

Ulele is at 1810 North Highland Avenue, Tampa, FL 33602, in Tampa Heights on the Riverwalk. It sits next to Water Works Park, about 400 yards from the Straz Center for the Performing Arts.

### Is Ulele Restaurant Tampa Florida the Same as the Airport Location?

No, the airport Ulele is a second location in Airside C at Tampa International Airport. Searching ulele restaurant tampa most likely means the river restaurant at 1810 North Highland Avenue. The Columbia Restaurant Group runs other restaurants in Florida cities, but those aren't Ulele.

### Do I Need a Reservation at Ulele?

I'd say yes, especially for patio and waterfront tables at sunset. Call 813-999-4952 or book through OpenTable. Parties of 7 or more should call, and groups of 20 or more should use 813-310-3701 or groups@Ulele.com.

### What Are Ulele's Hours?

Ulele is open for lunch and dinner daily. Hours are Sunday through Thursday 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. and Friday and Saturday 11 a.m. to 11 p.m. It's closed on Thanksgiving and Christmas, so check before you go.

### What Is the Dress Code at Ulele?

The atmosphere is casual elegance, and formal is fine. Men must wear sleeves. If you're dressed more relaxed than they want for the main dining rooms, you may be seated outdoors instead.

## Final Thoughts

What won me over at Ulele Tampa was the whole setting: a 1903 water works building, a huge barbacoa grill and beer you can't get anywhere else, all with the Hillsborough River right there. Water Works Park next door makes it feel like an outing, not just a meal.

My big planning tip is simple: call ahead, wear sleeves and plan your parking before you leave. Do those three things and the evening runs smoothly. Then walk the river and enjoy it. 🌅

# 7 Things to Do on Saturday in Tampa, and Which Ones Clash

If you are looking for things to do on Saturday in Tampa, you will find a long list of attractions, and most of them will not fit into one day. I tested this on Saturday, October 3, 2026. I went around, walked, and asked questions. I did not attend every event, and I am not going to pretend I stood in rooms I did not stand in. What follows is what I could confirm, what I would book, and where the day falls apart if you try to do too much of it. 🌸

![Tampa skyline seen from the Hillsborough River at midday](https://images.pexels.com/photos/11665707/pexels-photo-11665707.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Connor Scott McManus](https://www.pexels.com/@connorscottmcmanus) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/pier-and-skyscrapers-on-horizon-11665707/)*

## Short on Time?

If you have one weekend day to spend in Tampa, Saturday splits into a morning, an afternoon, and a night. The afternoon and night have a few conflicts you should know about before you buy anything.

- **Morning:** Sensory Saturday at the Museum of Science and Industry, 8 to 10 a.m., needs a reservation. Book it first if it fits your day.
- **Midday:** The Tampa Orchid Club expo runs 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. at Northdale Park. Scaradise at the Florida State Fairgrounds runs 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. Pick one.
- **Afternoon or night:** ZooTampa's Creatures of the Night ran 4 to 10 p.m. on October 3. The Lightning played at 7 p.m. ET, with a blue-carpet arrival from 3:45 to 4:30 p.m. The zoo and the carpet are on opposite sides of the city, so you cannot do both well.
- **Free:** The Riverwalk is free and open all the time. The Ybor streetcar is a fair way to get between downtown and Seventh Avenue.
- **Before you buy:** Check the date on the listing. Some pricing and hours I found did not agree with each other, and I have said so below.

## 1. Start Early: Sensory Saturday at MOSI

![Museum of Science and Industry entrance on East Fowler Avenue in Tampa](https://images.pexels.com/photos/18498207/pexels-photo-18498207.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Jimmy Liao](https://www.pexels.com/@jimmy-liao-3615017) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/entrance-to-the-staff-washroom-at-the-taipei-railway-workshop-museum-18498207/)*

The only Saturday morning I could tie to a clock and a city date was Sensory Saturday at the Museum of Science and Industry. The City of Tampa listed it for Saturday, October 3, from 8 a.m. to 10 a.m. The museum is at 4801 E. Fowler Avenue, in the Terrace Park neighborhood, and it is an in-person event.

This is the one I would plan around if someone in your group needs a quieter start. MOSI built the morning with the Center for Autism and Related Disabilities at USF. The museum lowers the lights, reduces noise, opens before regular hours, and offers hands-on activities, exhibits, and a sensory-friendly planetarium show. The point is that the building is calmer when fewer people are in it.

Here are the parts that matter before you go:

- **Registration is required.** Walking up at 8:15 because someone said Saturday is how you end up circling a parking lot on Fowler.
- **The price I was given for non-members was $7 in advance.** I also saw a listing that said $7 to $10. Confirm the price at checkout instead of trusting either number. Museum members are free.
- **Tickets are non-refundable unless MOSI cancels them, and they cannot be moved to another date.** Read that twice if your plans are shaky.
- **You can stay after 10 a.m.** and keep using the exhibits, but the sensory-friendly part of the morning ends at 10.

One warning. A museum listing I looked at included a December 5 date for the program. The October 3 date came from the city. Confirm the exact day with the city or the museum before you plan your morning around it.

## 2. Tampa Orchid Club Expo at Northdale Park

![Orchid display table at a Tampa Orchid Club show at Northdale Park](https://images.pexels.com/photos/8280980/pexels-photo-8280980.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Quang Nguyen Vinh](https://www.pexels.com/@quang-nguyen-vinh-222549) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/hanging-plant-with-yellow-flowers-8280980/)*

The Tampa Orchid Club held its expo on Saturday, October 3, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. at Northdale Park, 15510 Hooting Owls Place. Entry was $8, and that includes a raffle ticket. If you say "Cattleya" at check-in, they give you another one. I liked that small detail. American Orchid Society judged plants were on display, and the club was still asking for trophy sponsors at $30 and for volunteers.

This is a club show, not a theme-park production. It has the feel of a Saturday that somebody in the neighborhood put together with real care. If you like plants, or you want a slow afternoon that is not a line for a ride, it is the most relaxed ticket I found. It is also a Saturday-only kind of thing. You could not do it in July.

It closes at 4 p.m., which matters for the rest of the day. If you go, plan to be out of the building before the late afternoon crowd arrives anywhere else.

## 3. Scaradise at the Florida State Fairgrounds

![Florida State Fairgrounds entrance on U.S. Highway 301 in Tampa](https://images.pexels.com/photos/34521712/pexels-photo-34521712.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Caio Cezar](https://www.pexels.com/@caiospil) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/cars-on-miami-highway-during-daytime-34521712/)*

Scaradise was the other 10 a.m. Saturday opening, running until 7 p.m. at the Florida State Fairgrounds. The address is 4800 U.S. Highway 301 North, and you enter from U.S. 301. The event had celebrity guests, autographs, photo ops, vendors, and horror merchandise. Admission was listed as a range from $35 to $80, with kids 10 and under free. Parking was $10 if you bought it ahead and $12 at the gate.

Be careful with the pricing. The range I saw is the spread across the tickets, but I did not get a clear breakdown of which price belongs to which day. Check the exact day you plan to attend before you buy.

The bigger practical problem is the property itself. The Fairgrounds is large, with multiple gates and facilities, including the amphitheater, the equestrian center, TECO Arena, Cracker Country, and an expo hall. If you tell your phone you are going to "the fairgrounds," you can end up at the right property and the wrong gate. Look up which gate the event uses before you leave.

Scaradise and the orchid show do not work as one Saturday. The orchids close at 4. Scaradise runs until 7 and wants its own afternoon.

## 4. Busch Gardens Spooktacular

![Busch Gardens Tampa Bay entrance decorated for Spooktacular](https://images.pexels.com/photos/5859418/pexels-photo-5859418.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Charles Parker](https://www.pexels.com/@charles-parker) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/yard-decorated-with-gravestones-on-halloween-5859418/)*

Spooktacular at Busch Gardens runs on Saturdays and Sundays from September 12 through November 1, so October 3 fell inside that window. The daytime part is the family version of Halloween: a parade, trick-or-treating, and story time. It is a whole Saturday, not a quick stop. 🎃

Howl-O-Scream is a separate ticket. It is not included with regular admission, so do not assume your park ticket covers the scare event. The scare event runs September 11 through October 31, 2026. I did not get a gate time for October 3 that I trust, so check the park's schedule for the day you go.

If your Saturday is built around the park, you probably do not have time for an orchid show or a late zoo visit. Pick one major ticketed thing and keep the rest of the day flexible.

## 5. Creatures of the Night at ZooTampa

![ZooTampa at Lowry Park entrance at dusk during a fall event](https://images.pexels.com/photos/21613024/pexels-photo-21613024.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Jr  Satilite](https://www.pexels.com/@jr-satilite-1139874) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/illuminated-carousel-at-theme-park-in-evening-21613024/)*

Creatures of the Night was the zoo's Saturday night. ZooTampa listed the event for October 3 from 4 p.m. to 10 p.m. at 1101 W. Sligh Avenue. It is billed for all ages, with characters, animals, spooky stuff, and creepy food. Members and Zoo Fun ticket holders are free for that seasonal event. 🦁

Read the blockouts closely. The dates the zoo named for membership blockouts were October 10, 17, and 24. Those are later Saturdays, not October 3. A membership that works on October 3 might not work the same way on the later nights. People remember "free for members" and then apply it to whatever night they are visiting. Check the date on your own ticket.

The zoo's posted hours did not agree with each other. One notice said Saturday's Creatures of the Night ran 9:30 a.m. to 10 p.m., and another said the zoo was open 9:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. The event's own listing for the night was 4 to 10 p.m., so I went by that. Do not assume the zoo is open late on any other day because a Saturday label is still showing somewhere. I also do not have a general-admission price I trust, so I am leaving that out.

The zoo sits on its own side of town. Give yourself real travel time before a game or any other evening plan in the area.

## 6. Lightning Home Opener at Benchmark International Arena

![Benchmark International Arena on Channelside Drive in downtown Tampa on game night](https://images.pexels.com/photos/8974845/pexels-photo-8974845.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Ron Lach](https://www.pexels.com/@ron-lach) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/man-in-white-ice-hockey-jersey-playing-hockey-8974845/)*

The Lightning were the other Saturday night, and the team's game-day information was clearer than the zoo's. The game was Capitals at Lightning, at 7 p.m. ET, at Benchmark International Arena, 401 Channelside Drive. The team listed TV coverage on The Spot on Tampa Bay 66 with pregame at 6 p.m., and radio on 102.5. It was the home opener, and the team had a blue-carpet arrival from 3:45 to 4:30 p.m. on Ford Thunder Alley. They were also selling a 30th-anniversary Ice Palace puck inside the building. 🏒

For food and drinks before or after, the team points people to Sparkman Wharf at 615 Channelside. That is a practical suggestion, and a good one if you want to eat outside before the game. The area around the arena gets busy on game nights, so give yourself time to walk over.

The conflict is the timing. The carpet ran until 4:30 p.m., and the zoo's Creatures of the Night started at 4 p.m. on the other side of the city. If you want the carpet and the zoo in the same afternoon, you will be rushing one of them. Pick one, or accept that you will be late for the other.

I did not see the game's final score, and I am not going to make one up. What I can tell you is that the building and the area around it are a real part of a Saturday night downtown, even if you do not follow hockey.

## 7. Things to Do on Saturday in Tampa for Free: Riverwalk and Ybor

![Tampa Riverwalk in downtown Tampa with the Hillsborough River and palm trees](https://images.pexels.com/photos/6416111/pexels-photo-6416111.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Quang Nguyen Vinh](https://www.pexels.com/@quang-nguyen-vinh-222549) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/residential-buildings-and-palms-on-riverside-in-modern-city-6416111/)*

If your budget is zero and your schedule is loose, this is the part of the day I would keep. The Riverwalk is free, and the Friends of the Riverwalk list it as open 24 hours. You can start at the corner of Beneficial Drive and Channelside, or at Armature Works. Either way, a Saturday on the path is a walk through parks, not a ticketed festival.

Curtis Hixon is the big park on the path, with fountains and a playground. Farther north, Julian B. Lane has courts and a water playground. Armature Works is an old trolley barn with a food hall full of local restaurants, and it is a good place to stop for lunch on the way.

The other free move is the streetcar. It is the easiest way I found to get from downtown toward Ybor without a car. The ride is short, and you can get off on Seventh Avenue. Seventh is brick, with cigar shops, the Columbia Restaurant, and La Segunda, which has been baking in the same place for a long time. The chickens are the part you do not buy. They wander around the area, and you will see them whether or not you planned to.

Saturday on this route is a stroll, not a show. Plan on walking, eating, and looking around, and you will have a good afternoon without spending much. 🚋

## Useful Things to Know

Parking is the first thing people get wrong. The Fairgrounds, the zoo, Busch Gardens, and the arena each have their own parking situation, and most of them charge. Look up the parking for each place before you leave, especially if you are combining two of them in one day.

Timing is the second thing. A Saturday in Tampa is not one thing. It is a morning event, a midday event, and a night event, and a lot of the best ones are only open for part of that. Before you book a second ticket, check when the first one ends and how long the drive is.

Prices and hours change. Some of the numbers I found did not match across listings. The MOSI price ranged from $7 to $10 across the listings I looked at. The Fairgrounds range was $35 to $80, and I could not get the day-by-day split. The zoo's posted hours conflicted. In each case, confirm the exact number on the day you go.

Dates matter more than you think. The zoo's membership blockouts fall on later Saturdays. Howl-O-Scream is a separate ticket. The Busch Gardens scare event has its own date range. Read the date on your ticket, not just the event name.

The last thing: do not try to do everything. The cool places and the events are real, and they are good. But one Saturday is not big enough for all of them, and the people who have the worst time are the ones who schedule three things that cannot all happen.

## FAQ

### What are the best things to do on Saturday in Tampa?

It depends on what kind of day you want. For a quieter morning, the sensory-friendly hours at the Museum of Science and Industry are the most focused option I found. For a night out, the zoo's Creatures of the Night or a Lightning game are the big ones. For something free, the Riverwalk and a streetcar ride to Ybor are the easiest choices. Pick one anchor and build the rest around it.

### Do I need to book anything in advance on a Saturday in Tampa?

For the MOSI Sensory Saturday, yes. Registration is required, and the tickets are non-refundable unless the museum cancels them. The Fairgrounds, zoo, and arena events also had advance ticket options, so buy ahead if you want a specific time. The Riverwalk and the streetcar do not need reservations.

### Is there anything free to do on a Saturday in Tampa?

Yes. The Riverwalk is free and open 24 hours, with parks along the way. The streetcar gives you a cheap way to get from downtown to Ybor. Seventh Avenue in Ybor is also worth a walk, even if you do not spend any money there. These are the easiest options if you want to keep the day flexible.

### Can I visit the zoo and the Lightning game on the same Saturday?

Only if you accept that you will be rushed. The zoo's Creatures of the Night ran 4 to 10 p.m. on October 3, and the Lightning's blue-carpet arrival ran 3:45 to 4:30 p.m. on Ford Thunder Alley. The zoo sits on the other side of the city from the arena. If you want both, you would need to skip the carpet or arrive late to the zoo.

### What time does Scaradise start and end?

On the day I was looking at, Scaradise ran from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. at the Florida State Fairgrounds, which you enter from U.S. 301. Confirm the day you plan to attend, because pricing and schedule can vary by day. Look up which gate the event uses before you drive out.

### How much does parking cost at the Florida State Fairgrounds?

For Scaradise, parking was listed at $10 if you bought it ahead and $12 at the gate. The Fairgrounds is a big property, so make sure you know which gate the event uses and that you enter from U.S. 301.

### Do I need a separate ticket for Howl-O-Scream at Busch Gardens?

Yes. Howl-O-Scream is a separate ticket and is not included with regular admission. The scare event runs September 11 through October 31, 2026, and the Spooktacular daytime events run Saturdays and Sundays through November 1. Check the date on the ticket you buy.

### Are the Riverwalk and the streetcar good options for a rainy Saturday?

They are better on a dry day. The Riverwalk is outdoors, and the streetcar is a short ride between stops, so if the weather turns, I would pick an indoor option like the museum or the food hall at Armature Works. Check the forecast before you commit to a long walk.

## Final Thoughts

Saturday in Tampa is a good day to be in the city, but it is not a good day to try to do everything. The best version I found was a single anchor, something that needs a ticket or a reservation, plus a free stop that does not need a schedule. Start early if you need the sensory-friendly morning, pick one of the midday or night events, and keep the Riverwalk or a streetcar ride for whatever time is left.

The places are real, and most of them are worth your time. The trick is to choose the one you actually want, check the date and the hours on the day you go, and leave room for the parts of Tampa that do not come with a ticket.

body:
# Things to Do in Tampa This Weekend: Free Walks, Ticketed Picks, and What to Skip

If you are searching for things to do in Tampa this weekend, the first thing to know is that the city does not offer one weekend. It offers several, and they rarely fit in the same two days. I was in town on October 3 and 4, and I spent that stretch sorting out a pile of dated events that started at different times in different parts of the area. Most of those are over now. What is left, and what runs regardless of the calendar, is what I would use for the weekend of October 10 and 11. Tampa has plenty of attractions, and the fun is still here. You just have to pick. 🌴

![Tampa Riverwalk at dusk looking toward downtown skyline](https://images.pexels.com/photos/39737894/pexels-photo-39737894.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Trev W. Adams](https://www.pexels.com/@trev-takes-photos) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/stunning-philadelphia-skyline-view-from-river-39737894/)*

## Short on Time?

- **Walk the Riverwalk.** It is free, it is open all the time, and it is the easiest way to see the water. Start early or go at sunset.
- **Ride the TECO Line Streetcar to Ybor.** The streetcar is free and comes every 15 minutes. Ybor's streets are the best place in town to see the chickens. 🐓
- **Pick one ticketed place for the day.** The Florida Aquarium works well on a weekend morning. Busch Gardens' Spooktacular works on a weekend afternoon. Raprager Farms is a drive, so only go if you want to spend the whole day on it.
- **Skip Creatures of the Night at ZooTampa this Saturday.** October 10 is one of the nights the zoo has blocked out.
- **Check hours and prices before you leave.** Almost everything on this list changes with the season, the day, or the latest notice from the place itself.

## 1. Things to Do in Tampa This Weekend: Walk the Riverwalk

The Riverwalk is the free default, and I would start here if you only have an hour. It is 2.6 miles, and the path is open 24 hours. You walk along the Hillsborough River toward the Garrison Channel, past the fountains and parks near downtown. Curtis Hixon, at 600 N. Ashley Drive, sits right on the route. It is about 8 acres with fountains, a playground, and a dog park, so it works well for kids or for anyone who wants to sit down.

The one thing people get wrong is where the walk starts. Descriptions differ. Some put the start at Heights Market in Armature Works and run the path to Sparkman Wharf. Others start at Beneficial Drive and Channelside Drive and run just past Armature Works. Pick the end closest to where you park. Either way you get the river, the bridges, and the boats.

Two rules matter. Fishing is not allowed on the path. Drinks are only allowed in an approved specialty cup, and only inside the cup zone. Plan your coffee accordingly. Parking depends on which end you use, so check a map before you pick a spot.

![Riverwalk path along the Hillsborough River with a fountain and downtown buildings](https://images.pexels.com/photos/34761559/pexels-photo-34761559.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Allen Boguslavsky](https://www.pexels.com/@allen-boguslavsky-1344061) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/winter-scene-at-chicago-river-with-iconic-skyline-34761559/)*

## 2. Ride the TECO Line Streetcar to Ybor

The TECO Line Streetcar is free, runs seven days a week, has 11 stations, and comes every 15 minutes. It goes from downtown through the Channel District to Ybor. The ride is short, and it works better than a tour. You do not need a plan once you are on it. Get off at the station that looks interesting and walk.

Ybor is where the chickens are. They have been wandering those streets for more than a century, and the neighborhood is a bird sanctuary by city ordinance. You will see them on sidewalks and in the shade. Do not feed them, do not chase them, and watch where you step. The area gets busy at night, so if you want a quieter afternoon, go before dinner.

Bayshore Boulevard is the other no-ticket walk worth a Saturday morning. It is a 10-foot-wide path along the water, and it is billed as the largest continuous sidewalk in the country. It is flat, shaded in spots, and full of people walking dogs, running, and pushing strollers. Bring water.

![TECO Line Streetcar on the tracks in Ybor City with historic brick buildings](https://images.pexels.com/photos/12181717/pexels-photo-12181717.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Connor Scott McManus](https://www.pexels.com/@connorscottmcmanus) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/grayscale-photo-of-a-city-street-12181717/)*

## 3. Florida Aquarium: Morning Is the Right Time

The Florida Aquarium is at 701 Channelside Drive. It is the best ticketed option if you want a regular indoor visit that does not take the whole day. When I visited, it was open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Confirm those hours before you go, because they can change. 🐢

The habitat they lead with is Heart of the Sea. You will see a loggerhead sea turtle, a Maori wrasse, and a blue speckled grouper. Penguin greetings, stingray feeding, and sloth feeding are add-ons. I did not get a current ticket price during my check, so look at the aquarium's own ticket page before you plan a family budget.

A morning visit is the version I would pick this weekend. It lets you finish early and still have the afternoon for the Riverwalk or the streetcar. Later in October, the aquarium has other events: Parents' Time Off is October 17, a sensory hour is October 25 from 8 to 9 a.m., and Guppyween runs October 24 through 31. Those dates are after this weekend, but they are worth knowing if you are planning ahead.

![Florida Aquarium exhibit with a loggerhead sea turtle swimming in a large blue tank](https://images.pexels.com/photos/24906366/pexels-photo-24906366.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Wijs (Wise)](https://www.pexels.com/@wijs-wise-136435282) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/hatchling-of-sea-turtle-swimming-in-sea-24906366/)*

## 4. Busch Gardens Spooktacular: Daytime Halloween Without the Scares

Busch Gardens has a few Halloween layers, and it helps to know which is which. Spooktacular runs Saturdays and Sundays from September 12 through November 1. It includes a parade, trick-or-treating, and story time. It is the daytime, kid-friendly version of the season, and it fits a family afternoon.

The park also runs a separately ticketed scare event from September 11 through October 31, 2026. Howl-O-Scream is the name the park uses for that event, and it is not included with regular admission. The dates I saw for the scare event did not carry the Howl-O-Scream name, so check the exact dates and what your ticket covers before you buy anything. Do not assume one ticket works for both.

My advice is simple. Pick Spooktacular for a daytime visit, or pick the scare event for an evening, but not both on the same afternoon if you also have a game or a long drive. Busch Gardens is a full day, and a split schedule wears people out fast. 🎃

![Busch Gardens Tampa Bay entrance with a Halloween parade float and costumed characters](https://images.pexels.com/photos/30975288/pexels-photo-30975288.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Drinu Cutajar](https://www.pexels.com/@drinu-cutajar-347725497) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/vibrant-illuminated-carnival-parade-float-at-night-30975288/)*

## 5. Raprager Farms in Odessa: The Drive Is the Real Decision

Raprager Farms is a real fall destination, but it is not in Tampa. The address is 16907 Boy Scout Road in Odessa, 33556. It is in the area, and it is a drive, so think of it as a separate trip rather than an add-on to a downtown afternoon.

The farm's season runs from September through November. Sundays are listed 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. Typically included are pumpkins, hayrides, animals, a bounce pillow, a corn pit, Fort Merlin, a passion fruit maze, and a mechanical bull. Axe throwing, pony rides, gem mining, and a zip line are extra. When I looked, the zip line was unavailable pending a state inspection. Check whether that has changed before you plan around it.

Night scares stay in a marked area and do not start until after 6 p.m. on select October dates. Do not assume October 11 is one of those dates without checking. Ticket prices are the other thing to verify. One listing I came across said tickets start at $19, but the farm itself told me that inclusions vary and that I should check the current ticket options. Trust the farm's current options over any number passed along to you.

Raprager is cool if you have a whole Sunday and a car. It is less fun if you want to see three things in one afternoon.

![Pumpkin patch and hayride at a Florida farm in autumn with a red barn in the background](https://images.pexels.com/photos/33881605/pexels-photo-33881605.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Alexas Fotos](https://www.pexels.com/@alexasfotos) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/vibrant-fall-pumpkins-in-rustic-wooden-crate-33881605/)*

## Useful Things to Know

**Know which events are over.** Last weekend had a lot going on: Sensory Saturday at MOSI, the Tampa Orchid Club expo at Northdale Park, and the Scaradise horror convention at the Florida State Fairgrounds. Those ran October 3 and 4. If you are planning for this weekend, do not count on them. Check each organizer's site for what is running now.

**Sensory Saturday dates did not match.** The city's calendar listed Sensory Saturday for October 3, but MOSI's own dates pointed to a different date. If you want a sensory-friendly morning at MOSI in the future, check MOSI directly, register in advance, and do not just show up.

**ZooTampa's Creatures of the Night has blockout nights.** The zoo listed October 10, 17, and 24 as nights without the event. That means this Saturday is off. The zoo's notices also disagreed about hours, with one saying 9:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. and another saying 9:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Do not plan an evening around the shorter one, and confirm before you drive over.

**Pick one big thing per day.** Tampa is spread out. The Aquarium is downtown, Busch Gardens is north of the river, and Raprager is in Odessa. Mix the activities you care about most: one major outing and a couple of free walks. Anything more and you will spend the afternoon in your car.

**Check today's hours, not last week's.** Hours and event schedules change, and some of what you read online is out of date. Look at each place's page on the day you go, especially if you are heading to a holiday-themed event. Things that were open on Saturday may have a different schedule today.

**Parking changes by spot.** Downtown and Channel District parking shifts with events. The Riverwalk's parking depends on which end you use. Give yourself extra time on a crowded Saturday.

**Bring water and shade.** Florida in October is still warm, and both the Riverwalk and Bayshore are open to the sun for long stretches.

**Plan around sports days.** Tampa's stadium and arena days change traffic and crowds. I do not have this weekend's schedule, so check the team's site before you commit to a downtown afternoon.

**Expect the day to be shorter than you think.** Two ticketed things and a walk is a full day. Three ticketed things is a plan that falls apart by the second stop.

## FAQ

### What are the best free things to do in Tampa this weekend?

The Riverwalk is the best free choice. It is 2.6 miles, open 24 hours, and runs along the Hillsborough River. The TECO Line Streetcar is also free and goes from downtown to Ybor. Bayshore Boulevard is a good flat walk for a morning. Curtis Hixon, at 600 N. Ashley Drive, is a free park with fountains, a playground, and a dog park.

### Is the TECO Line Streetcar really free?

As far as I know, yes. It is free, runs seven days a week, has 11 stations, and comes every 15 minutes. I would still check current service before you build a schedule around it.

### Where does the Tampa Riverwalk start?

Descriptions differ. Some put the start at Heights Market in Armature Works and run to Sparkman Wharf. Others start at Beneficial Drive and Channelside Drive, just past Armature Works. Pick the end closest to your parking. Fishing is not allowed, and drinks must be in an approved specialty cup inside the cup zone.

### Can I bring my kids to the Florida Aquarium this weekend?

Yes. The aquarium is a good indoor option, especially in the morning. When I visited, it was open from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. at 701 Channelside Drive. Heart of the Sea, with a loggerhead, a Maori wrasse, and a blue speckled grouper, is the main habitat. Confirm hours and ticket prices before you go, because I did not get a current price.

### Is Spooktacular at Busch Gardens open this weekend?

Spooktacular is listed as running Saturdays and Sundays from September 12 through November 1, so it should be running on October 10 and 11. Check the park's calendar for exact times. The separate scare event, Howl-O-Scream, is a different ticket and is not included with regular admission.

### Do I need a car to do things in Tampa this weekend?

For the Riverwalk, the streetcar, and Bayshore, no. You can walk, use the streetcar, and get around downtown without a car. For Busch Gardens, the Aquarium, or Raprager Farms, you will likely want one. Raprager Farms is in Odessa, which is a drive from downtown.

### Is Creatures of the Night at ZooTampa open this Saturday?

Not on October 10. The zoo listed that night as a blockout, along with October 17 and 24. Check ZooTampa's current schedule for other nights, and confirm hours before you go, because the zoo's notices did not agree.

### What are some things to do in Tampa FL this weekend if I only have one day?

Start with a morning on the Riverwalk, then take the TECO Line Streetcar to Ybor for lunch and a look at the chickens. In the afternoon, choose one ticketed place, like the Florida Aquarium or Busch Gardens. That gives you a full day without rushing.

## Final Thoughts

The most common mistake with things to do in Tampa this weekend is treating the whole city like one long menu. The free walks and the streetcar will always be there. The ticketed places run on their own calendars, and the farm is in a different town. Pick one or two things, pay attention to hours and blockout nights, and leave room for a walk. If you try to do everything, you will spend the weekend in traffic. Keep it small, and the city does most of the work for you. That is the answer to things to do this weekend Tampa, and it holds up better than any checklist.

title: 5 Things to Know Before You Play TPC Tampa in Lutz
