# Yard House Tampa: 5 Things to Know Before You Go to Water Street

If you have typed yard house tampa into a search bar, you probably expected one of two things: a food-court version tucked inside a mall, or a second location out near the airport. I did too. That is how a lot of national chains land in this city. What I found is one restaurant, on Water Street across from Amalie Arena, at 450 Channelside Drive. I have been there enough to have opinions, and most of them are about the parts that trip people up: the address, the clock, and what happens on a Lightning night.

![Yard House Tampa on Water Street at 450 Channelside Drive, with Amalie Arena across the street](https://images.pexels.com/photos/13068511/pexels-photo-13068511.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Connor Scott McManus](https://www.pexels.com/@connorscottmcmanus) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/an-aerial-photography-of-houses-near-the-green-trees-under-the-blue-sky-and-white-clouds-13068511/)*

## Short on Time?

- **Address:** 450 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602. The restaurant calls itself "Tampa - Water Street." Put the street number in your rideshare app, not the neighborhood name.
- **Phone:** (813) 371-5495. Call this before you promise a large group a table.
- **Hours have two clocks.** On the Saturday I checked, the doors were listed open from 11:00 a.m. to 1:20 a.m., but ordering ahead and private dining stopped at 11:50 p.m. The door time is not the kitchen time.
- **Event nights change things.** Yard House warns that happy hour is not available on event dates and that hours can be affected. If you are coming for an arena game, check the day of.
- **Beer is the point.** The brand's pitch is a draft list it describes as 130 taps. Food is there and it is solid for a big group, but this is a beer-first room.
- **Groups are expected.** There is large party seating, private dining, curbside pickup, takeout, and delivery.
- **This is not a steakhouse.** If you are looking for a special-occasion steak dinner, go somewhere else.

🍺 That is the short version. The rest of this is the stuff I wish someone had told me before my first visit.

## 1. Find the Right Yard House Tampa Address

The first mistake people make is looking for a second Yard House in some other part of the Tampa Bay area. I know of no second official Tampa location. If a map pin puts you in Brandon or near International Plaza, I would not trust it over the Water Street address. Those pins are easy to get wrong, and the wrong one will cost you a drive.

The restaurant sits on Channelside Drive, but the development it belongs to is called Water Street, and most people use both names without thinking about it. That is where the confusion starts. Rideshare drivers see "Water Street" and sometimes drop you at the wrong corner of the development. The street address, 450 Channelside Drive, is the one that matters. Once you have it, the landmark helps: the restaurant faces Amalie Arena, so if you can see the arena, you are close.

I also want to be honest about what I did not confirm. I never got a parking garage name or a clear statement about parking costs from the restaurant, so I am not going to tell you where to park or what it costs. Plan for downtown parking the way you would for any busy block near a stadium. Leave early, and do not assume you can drop in and leave in ten minutes.

Once you are in the right building, the layout is simple. You can sit inside, where you get a view of the keg room, or outside on the patio, which the restaurant calls an energized beer garden. Both are good in different moods. Inside is louder in a way that feels like a bar. The patio is where you go when the weather is decent and the crowd is in a good mood.

![Yard House Tampa patio and beer garden on Water Street at dusk](https://images.pexels.com/photos/27623559/pexels-photo-27623559.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Donovan Kelly](https://www.pexels.com/@donovan-kelly-110228397) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-wooden-tray-with-several-beers-on-it-27623559/)*

## 2. Read the Hours as Two Clocks

This is the part I would tell anyone first. On the Saturday I checked, Yard House listed the restaurant open from 11:00 a.m. to 1:20 a.m. That same Saturday, ordering ahead and private dining were only available until 11:50 p.m. Those are different clocks, and they are not the same thing.

Here is why it matters. Say you get out of a late arena event and walk over thinking the full menu is still running because the sign says the place is open past midnight. You may be looking at a shorter order window than the posted close. I am not making up a last-call menu or a separate late-night menu. I am saying the restaurant itself gave me two times for two different things on the same day, and I would plan around the earlier one.

Happy hour is a separate problem. Yard House says happy hour is not available on event dates, and that hours may be affected. I never got a clock for happy hour that I felt good enough to write down as fact. I did see a schedule elsewhere that gave Monday through Thursday and Sunday as 11 a.m. to midnight, and Friday and Saturday as 11 a.m. to 1:20 a.m. The Saturday part matches what I was given directly. The weekday part I could not confirm the way I would like, so I would not plan a Tuesday around midnight without checking first.

My rule is simple. Call (813) 371-5495 or check the day of your visit, especially if you are coming for a specific game, a concert, or a weekend crowd. Do not write down one day and assume the other six work the same way.

![Yard House Tampa exterior sign on Channelside Drive during the evening](https://images.pexels.com/photos/31045433/pexels-photo-31045433.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [James Collington](https://www.pexels.com/@james-collington-2147687246) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/in-n-out-burger-sign-at-sunset-31045433/)*

## 3. Plan Around Arena Nights

Yard House is across from Amalie Arena, and that is the single biggest reason the restaurant is busy at the times people most want to be there. On a regular weekday afternoon the walk from the parking area is easy. On a Lightning night 🏒, the same block is a crowd, and the restaurant is already telling you that happy hour and hours can change for events.

This is the part I would think about before you leave home. If your group is going before a game, ask yourself whether you want a table at a set time or whether you are fine walking in and waiting. If you are going after a game, know that the kitchen and the bar will both be under pressure. I would not plan a long dinner that has to wrap by a specific time without leaving slack in the schedule.

If the wait looks bad when you arrive, curbside pickup and takeout are real options, and so is delivery if you are already staying in a downtown hotel and do not want to deal with Channelside traffic. None of that replaces a call ahead, but it gives you a backup plan that does not depend on finding a seat in the keg room.

I want to be clear that I am describing the restaurant's own warning here, not my guess about crowd sizes. The warning exists, and that is enough reason to plan for it.

![Crowd heading toward Amalie Arena on Channelside Drive before a game](https://images.pexels.com/photos/28128417/pexels-photo-28128417.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Adrien Olichon](https://www.pexels.com/@adrien-olichon-1257089) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-group-of-people-watching-a-hockey-game-on-a-screen-28128417/)*

## 4. Know What the Room Is Built For

Yard House is built for groups and for beer. The amenities I was told about include private dining, large party seating at this location, curbside pickup, ordering ahead, and delivery. That is a different setup from a quiet neighborhood bar. It is a big room that expects people to come in together and order a lot.

The draft list is the headline. The brand describes it as the world's largest selection of draft beer, with 130 taps. That is their claim, and I am passing it along as their pitch, not as something I counted myself. What I can tell you is that the keg room is the thing they want you to look at when you walk in. If you care about beer, plan to spend some time reading the list before you order.

On the food side, the restaurant describes American-style dishes. Another account I came across listed a long menu with dishes like poke nachos, a kurobuta pork burger, lobster garlic noodles, vampire tacos, and a queso dip. I am not going to promise any of those are on the menu the night you visit. Menus move, and a list someone else wrote a year ago is not a reliable guide to what is in the kitchen now. What I will say is that the food is meant to be shared and eaten with a drink in hand, not in the careful, plated way you would expect in a fine-dining room.

If you are bringing a mixed group, this is a good fit. Someone who wants a beer flight, someone who wants a burger, and someone who wants to split a few plates can all find something here without much negotiation. That is the real strength of a place like this.

![Yard House Tampa keg room and draft tap wall with the beer list behind the bar](https://images.pexels.com/photos/20883378/pexels-photo-20883378.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Daniel Januario](https://www.pexels.com/@daniel-januario-1127884405) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/man-hands-pouring-beer-20883378/)*

## 5. Don't File It with Steakhouses

People try to put this restaurant in the same mental folder as steakhouses and grills in town, and I think that is because of the word "house" and because downtown has so many hotel restaurants and old-school rooms nearby, places like the Bern's-style steakhouses that people treat as special occasions. That filing is wrong.

If someone in your group wants a quiet, formal steak dinner, this is the wrong place. You will get noise, classic rock, a big crowd, and a menu built around sharing. If someone wants a long beer list and a table that can handle a mixed group before or after a game, this is the right place. Knowing which one you are looking for will save you a lot of disappointment.

The same goes for the other things people sometimes assume are nearby. This is not a sushi counter, a Thai cafe, or an Italian trattoria. It is a big draft-beer restaurant across from the arena. Going in with the right expectation makes the whole evening better.

![Yard House Tampa dining room with a mix of tables and bar seating on a weekend evening](https://images.pexels.com/photos/6536617/pexels-photo-6536617.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Daria](https://www.pexels.com/@dubart) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-dimmed-lighted-restaurant-wine-glasses-on-counter-top-6536617/)*

## Useful Things to Know

**Parking and arrival.** I did not confirm a garage name or parking rates, so plan for downtown parking near the arena. Give yourself extra time on game nights 🚗. If you are using a rideshare, use the 450 Channelside Drive address and not just "Water Street."

**Hours on paper versus hours in practice.** The posted close and the order cutoff are not the same. On the Saturday I checked, ordering ahead and private dining ended at 11:50 p.m., even though the restaurant was listed open later. If you are planning a late meal, do not wait until the last hour to order.

**Happy hour on event dates.** Happy hour is not available on event dates, and the restaurant's own warning says so. Check before you plan around a discount.

**Large groups.** Large party seating is available at this location, but "available" does not mean "held for you." Call (813) 371-5495 before you promise a table to a big group, especially on a game night.

**Private dining.** Private dining exists, but it has its own cutoff. Ask about the window when you call so no one shows up expecting a room that is already closed for the night.

**Promotions.** I came across an Oktoberfest refill promotion that ran through October 25. I am not treating that as a standing price. Promotions end, and I would not plan a budget around one. If you want to know whether it is still running, ask when you call.

**Takeout and delivery.** If the dining room is packed, curbside pickup and takeout are real options. Delivery is also offered, which can be handy if you are staying downtown and do not want to deal with the traffic.

**What people get wrong.** The most common mistakes I have seen, or heard described, are going to the wrong address, assuming the posted closing time is the kitchen time, and showing up on an arena night with a large group and no plan. Each one is easy to avoid with a single phone call.

**Not a second location.** There is one Yard House in Tampa that I know of. If your map app shows a different one, double-check the address before you drive.

## FAQ

### Is there more than one Yard House Tampa location?

Not that I know of. The restaurant I am describing is at 450 Channelside Drive, on Water Street across from Amalie Arena. If a map shows a Yard House in Brandon or near International Plaza, I would trust the Water Street address instead, and call to confirm before you drive anywhere else.

### What is the address and phone number for Yard House Tampa?

The address is 450 Channelside Drive, Tampa, FL 33602. The phone number is (813) 371-5495. The restaurant calls the location "Tampa - Water Street," so the street address is the most useful detail to give a rideshare driver.

### What are the hours for yard house tampa?

On the Saturday I checked, the restaurant was listed open from 11:00 a.m. to 1:20 a.m., but ordering ahead and private dining were only available until 11:50 p.m. Hours can change, and happy hour is not available on event dates. I would call or check the day of your visit, especially if you are going on a weekday or a game night.

### Is happy hour at Yard House Tampa every day?

I would not assume so. The restaurant warns that happy hour is not available on event dates and that hours may be affected. I saw one schedule that gave weekday and weekend happy hour times, but I could not confirm the weekday part the way I would like. Ask when you call before you plan around a discount.

### Can I make a reservation for a large group at yard house tampa?

Large party seating is available at this location, and private dining is offered. I would call (813) 371-5495 before you promise anyone a table, particularly on an arena night. Ask about the private dining cutoff and whether your group size needs a specific arrangement.

### Is yard house tampa a good place for a special-occasion steak dinner?

No, not in my opinion. The restaurant is built around a large draft-beer list, a loud room, and a menu meant for sharing. If you want a quiet, formal steak dinner, look at a steakhouse instead. This place works better for a mixed group that wants beer and an easy meal before or after a game.

### Does yard house tampa offer takeout, curbside pickup, or delivery?

Yes. The restaurant names curbside pickup, ordering ahead, and delivery among its options. If the dining room is packed, takeout or curbside can save you a long wait. Delivery can be a good choice if you are staying downtown and do not want to deal with traffic.

### What is the best way to plan a visit to Yard House Tampa on a game night?

Give yourself extra time to park and walk over, because the block near Amalie Arena gets crowded. Call ahead for a large group, check whether happy hour is running, and decide before you leave whether you need a table or are fine with curbside if the wait gets long.

## Final Thoughts

Yard House Tampa is one building on Water Street, across from the arena, at 450 Channelside Drive. It is not a mall food court and it is not a second location out by the airport. If you go in knowing that, the rest is manageable: call ahead for a big group, read the hours as two separate clocks, and plan around game nights instead of hoping for the best.

It is a beer-first place with a loud room and a menu built for sharing. I would send a group there that wants a long draft list and an easy meal, and I would send someone else to a steakhouse if they want a quiet, formal dinner. The address is the first thing to get right, and the hours are the second. Get those two right and the rest of the night usually works out 🍻.

body:
# Texas de Brazil Tampa: 5 Things to Know Before You Sit Down at the Boy Scout Boulevard Churrascaria

Texas de Brazil Tampa is the churrascaria at 4112 West Boy Scout Boulevard in Westshore, and it is not the steakhouse a little farther down the same road. I live in Tampa and I have been asked about this restaurant enough times that I finally worked through the details: where it is, how the meat service works, what the meal costs, and the parts people trip over once they are inside. Most of the confusion comes down to the address and the rules, so that is where I started. This is the version I would give a friend who is about to make a reservation.

![Texas de Brazil Tampa storefront on West Boy Scout Boulevard in Westshore](https://images.pexels.com/photos/10769620/pexels-photo-10769620.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [kingsley li](https://www.pexels.com/@kingsley-li-159057939) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/people-walking-near-the-building-10769620/)*

## Short on Time? 🥩

If you only read this part, here is what matters.

- **The address:** 4112 West Boy Scout Boulevard, Tampa, FL 33607. Phone is 813.981.7157. It is not downtown, not Ybor, and not on Dale Mabry.
- **The meal:** 🍽️ Endless grilled meats brought to your table by gauchos, plus a salad area with salads, vegetables, imported cheeses, and specialty items. You can also choose a salad-area-only option at a lower price.
- **The price (when I last checked):** Dinner full service is $65.99. Salad area only is $33.99. Weekday lunch is $39.99 with salad area only at $23.99.
- **The token:** Green side means keep the meat coming. Turn it to the other side when you want a break.
- **Reservations:** 📞 Not required, but call ahead for a large party or a night when something big is happening nearby. Parties over 15 should call.
- **Parking:** 🚗 Self-parking is available. Confirm the address with your rideshare driver.
- **Leftovers:** You cannot box up the uneaten food from the meal. Plan on eating what you order.

## 1. Find Texas de Brazil Tampa on Boy Scout Boulevard

The first problem people run into is simply finding the right place. If you search for texas de brazil tampa fl, you will get a mix of listings, chain pages, and nearby restaurants, so it helps to know exactly what you are looking for. Texas de Brazil Tampa sits in the Westshore District, close to Tampa International Airport. International Plaza is nearby, and so is Raymond James Stadium, which is the other reason a lot of people end up on this stretch of road on a given night.

Westshore has more than one steakhouse along Boy Scout Boulevard. If all you remember is "the Brazilian place by the mall," you can easily pull into the wrong lot. The one you want is the churrascaria at 4112. The prime steakhouse a little farther along is a different restaurant with a different menu and a different experience. I have seen people get frustrated before they ever sat down, because they were standing in front of the wrong door, or because they were convinced the restaurant they had in mind was the one they were looking at.

If you are taking a rideshare, do not just say "Boy Scout and the mall." Give the driver the number, 4112 West Boy Scout Boulevard, and confirm it in the app before you get in. That one habit saves a lot of trouble on a busy evening, especially when a game or event is letting out at the stadium.

Texas de Brazil Tampa is also a good stop if you are working around a flight. It is close enough to the airport that a lot of people pick it as a last meal before a trip or a first meal after one. Just pay attention to the lunch and dinner windows, which I cover further down, so your plans match the hours.

![Boy Scout Boulevard in Westshore near International Plaza with traffic at dusk](https://images.pexels.com/photos/33464606/pexels-photo-33464606.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Abhishek  Navlakha](https://www.pexels.com/@navlakha) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/buffalo-wild-wings-on-las-vegas-boulevard-33464606/)*

## 2. How the Meat Service and the Token Actually Work

This is the part that makes the place feel different from a normal restaurant, and it is the part first-timers get wrong most often.

When you sit down, you choose either the standard menu or the vegetarian option. The vegetarian option costs less because you are using the salad area and not the meat service. You get a small token. The green side means you want meat. Turn it to the other side when you want the gauchos to pause. Turn it back when you want more. You can do that as often as you like.

The gauchos are the staff who carry long skewers of steak and other meats from table to table. Each one is holding a skewer in one hand and a knife in the other. Here is the detail that trips people up: the house rule is that you take the slice with the tongs on your plate, not with the fork you have been eating with. It is a hygiene rule, and it makes sense once you see the sequence, but when a skewer is hovering over your shoulder it is easy to grab the wrong utensil. Keep the tongs close and let the gaucho bring the meat to you.

You can ask for a lot of one cut, and nobody will think less of you for it. The one limit I would respect is not asking for an entire skewer when other diners are waiting on it. Be reasonable and the service stays smooth.

Not every cut is available all night. Availability depends on the location and on what is left on the grill. If a favorite is gone, ask a gaucho whether it is coming back. A popular item sometimes returns, and asking is free.

Drinks and desserts are handled by a different person from the one carrying the meat. If you only flag down the gaucho with the skewer, your drink order can sit there while you wait. Get the attention of the right server for the drink, and then get the meat.

Finally, go to the salad area early. The restaurant recommends going first so you can see what is out, then going back again later, because the salad area and the hot items are refreshed through the meal. People who skip the salad area until they are already full are passing up a big part of the price they paid. Treat it as a second course, not a side trip.

![Gaucho carving meat tableside at Texas de Brazil Tampa with diners and tongs](https://images.pexels.com/photos/9397270/pexels-photo-9397270.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Hayden Walker](https://www.pexels.com/@haydenplus1) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-person-slicing-barbecue-beef-brisket-9397270/)*

## 3. Prices, Hours, and Picking the Right Meal

I am putting these numbers down as they stood when I last checked. Prices and hours can change, and they can differ by location or during holidays, so treat this as a starting point and confirm before you go. The Tampa location is the only one I am talking about here.

**Dinner, full service:** $65.99
**Dinner, salad area only:** $33.99
**Weekday lunch, full service:** $39.99
**Weekday lunch, salad area only:** $23.99
**Weekend lunch:** priced like dinner, at $65.99 full service and $33.99 salad area only

Weekday lunch is the cheaper meal, and it runs Monday through Friday from 11am to 2pm. Weekend lunch is the dinner menu at dinner prices. It runs Saturday from 12pm to 4pm and Sunday from 11am to 4pm. Dinner hours are Monday through Thursday 5pm to 9:30pm, Friday 5pm to 10pm, Saturday 4pm to 10pm, and Sunday 4pm to 9pm.

If you are picking between lunch and dinner, the question is mostly about price and appetite. Weekday lunch is the best value if you can get there before 2pm. Weekend lunch is the better choice if you want the full dinner menu earlier in the day, particularly before an evening flight. I would not try to squeeze a weekday dinner visit into a tight schedule. Give yourself time to eat, use the salad area twice, and not feel rushed when the gauchos come back around.

Happy hour runs Monday through Friday from 4:30pm to 6pm. The house offers include domestic beers for $5, caipirinhas and the house cocktail for $7, glasses of the private-label wine for $8, and house martinis for $9. Those offers can vary and are not valid everywhere they are prohibited. Happy hour is a drink deal in that gap between lunch and dinner. It is not the same as full meat service, so do not show up at 3pm expecting the whole thing.

Here is what the listed price does not cover: alcohol, featured items, à la carte items, desserts, beverages, tax, and gratuity. Plan for those on top of the base price. The suggested gratuity is 18 to 20 percent if you were happy with the service, which is a normal range for a sit-down meal like this, but the decision is yours.

Children are priced differently. Ages 2 and under eat free with a full-price adult meal. Ages 3 to 5 are $5.00. Ages 6 to 12 are half price. Those child prices apply with a full-price meal.

For payment, they take Visa, MasterCard, American Express, and Discover, along with cash. They do not accept personal or company checks. I would bring a card as your main option and keep some cash for the tip.

Thanksgiving is a special case. On Thanksgiving Day, Thursday, November 26, the restaurant starts serving at 11:00am on the dinner menu at dinner pricing, with some holiday classics. I do not have a full calendar of holiday hours for Tampa, so for any other holiday, call 813.981.7157 before you plan around it.

![Dining room at Texas de Brazil Tampa with the salad area and a menu card on a table](https://images.pexels.com/photos/20883787/pexels-photo-20883787.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Daniel Januario](https://www.pexels.com/@daniel-januario-1127884405) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/close-up-of-a-table-full-of-seafood-dishes-20883787/)*

## 4. Reservations, Big Groups, and What to Wear

Reservations are not required. Still, I would make one if you can, especially on a Friday or Saturday night or on a night when something is happening at Raymond James or in the district. A busy night can mean a long wait, and some locations are difficult to get into without booking ahead. I would not walk up at 6:30 on a Saturday and assume a seat will be waiting.

If your party is over 15 people, call the restaurant or submit an event request rather than trying to fit everyone in on a standard booking. Private dining is available for up to 40 guests. Patio dining is also available, which is nice on a mild evening.

For a buyout or a private room, plan on a phone conversation. I did not come away with a room diagram for the Tampa location, so do not assume you can see the layout from a photo. Ask about audio/visual rental and buyout options when you call, and get the details in writing if the event matters.

On dress, the restaurant recommends smart or business casual, but it does not enforce a formal dress code as long as clothing is reasonable and not offensive. Ordinary shirt-and-shoes rules still apply. Offensive graphics are the line they care about. It is not a jacket-required room, and it is not a beach-day buffet either.

![Patio dining area at Texas de Brazil Tampa on a mild evening](https://images.pexels.com/photos/33347950/pexels-photo-33347950.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Lucas Silva dos Santos](https://www.pexels.com/@lucasarleta) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/charming-outdoor-dining-with-red-umbrellas-in-toronto-33347950/)*

## 5. Leftovers, Dietary Questions, and Other Surprises

This is the section where I see the most disappointment, so I want to be direct about it.

You cannot take a box of uneaten salad-area food, meats, or sides home from the dining room. The price you pay is for the meal you eat there. Desserts may be boxed. If you want food to go, that is a separate order. Tampa offers to-go orders for pickup at the Boy Scout Boulevard location, and those are cooked to order. Catering is available and asks for at least five hours of notice, and it is aimed at groups of five or more. I would not promise a guest that the dining-room price includes a second meal in a container, because it does not.

Corkage is available where state law allows. It is $20 per 750ml bottle of wine, with a limit of two bottles, and no bottles of liquor. Large-format corkage is a question for the restaurant itself.

Dietary needs are a real consideration, so here is what I would tell a friend. The salad area is the vegetarian and vegan path through the meal. Several items are gluten-free, and the restaurant points guests to its nutrition information for details. Tell a manager about any allergies before or during the visit, not after the food arrives.

On halal, be careful. The lamb is bought halal, but it is cooked on the same skewers as everything else, including pork. So the cooked lamb is not considered halal. If that matters to you or your group, that is a clear reason to choose a different meal, and it is better to know before you sit down. The restaurant also does not serve kosher meat.

Gift cards bought in the U.S. are not redeemable at international locations, with the exception of Aruba. That is not a Tampa issue, but people who travel sometimes ask about it.

![Salad area at Texas de Brazil Tampa with vegetables, imported cheeses, and specialty items on display](https://images.pexels.com/photos/18303019/pexels-photo-18303019.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Matheus Alves](https://www.pexels.com/@monstro) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/bowl-of-vegetarian-salad-18303019/)*

## Useful Things to Know

**Parking:** Self-parking is available. I did not find valet pricing, a garage name, or a validation rule for the Tampa location, so I am not going to make one up. Plan for the self-park lot and leave a little extra time on a busy night, especially if there is a stadium event.

**Timing:** Weekday lunch closes at 2pm, and weekday dinner does not start until 5pm. That gap is where happy hour lives. If you are coming from the airport, weekend lunch is usually the most flexible option, since it runs later and is priced at the dinner rate.

**Pace:** Do not rush the meal. Go to the salad area early, come back, use the token as you like, and give yourself time between courses. People who try to eat fast tend to miss the good cuts that come around later.

**Payment:** Bring a card. Keep some cash handy. Personal and company checks are not accepted.

**Wait times:** On a busy weekend night, expect a wait if you did not book. Calling ahead gives you a much better shot at a clean start to the evening.

**Address check:** Before you drive over, double check 4112 West Boy Scout Boulevard. The name of the nearby mall is not enough to find this one.

## FAQ

### Where exactly is Texas de Brazil Tampa, FL?

Texas de Brazil Tampa is at 4112 West Boy Scout Boulevard, Tampa, FL 33607. It is in the Westshore District near Tampa International Airport, with International Plaza and Raymond James Stadium nearby. It is not in downtown Tampa, Ybor City, or on Dale Mabry. The nearby steakhouse along Boy Scout Boulevard is a separate restaurant, so use the address number when you get directions.

### Do I need a reservation for Texas de Brazil Tampa?

Reservations are not required, but I would book one, especially on Friday or Saturday nights or on a night with a big event nearby. Call 813.981.7157 for a reservation. If your party is over 15, call the restaurant or submit an event request instead of relying on a standard booking.

### How much does Texas de Brazil Tampa cost?

When I last checked, dinner full service was $65.99 and the salad-area-only option was $33.99. Weekday lunch was $39.99 for full service and $23.99 for salad area only. Prices do not include alcohol, featured or à la carte items, desserts, beverages, tax, or gratuity. Confirm current pricing before you go, since it can change.

### What are the hours for the Texas de Brazil Tampa location?

Weekday lunch runs Monday through Friday from 11am to 2pm. Weekend lunch runs Saturday from 12pm to 4pm and Sunday from 11am to 4pm. Dinner runs Monday through Thursday from 5pm to 9:30pm, Friday from 5pm to 10pm, Saturday from 4pm to 10pm, and Sunday from 4pm to 9pm. Happy hour is Monday through Friday from 4:30pm to 6pm. On Thanksgiving Day, service starts at 11:00am on the dinner menu. Call before any other holiday.

### Can I take leftovers home from Texas de Brazil?

No. You cannot box up uneaten food from the meal. Desserts may be boxed. If you want food to take home, you need a separate to-go order for pickup or catering, which requires at least five hours' notice and is aimed at groups of five or more. The dining-room price is for the meal you eat there.

### Is there a dress code at Texas de Brazil Tampa?

There is no enforced dress code. The restaurant recommends smart or business casual, and ordinary shirt-and-shoes rules apply. Offensive graphics are the main thing they do not allow. It is not a jacket-required place, but it is also not a casual beach setting.

### Is there a vegetarian option at Texas de Brazil Tampa?

Yes. You can choose the vegetarian option when you sit down, which uses the salad area instead of the meat service and costs less. The salad area includes salads, vegetables, imported cheeses, and specialty items. Several items are gluten-free, and you can ask a manager about allergies or ingredients before you order.

### Is the lamb at Texas de Brazil Tampa halal?

The lamb is bought halal, but it is cooked on the same skewers as the other meats, including pork. For that reason, the cooked lamb is not considered halal. If that matters to you, plan accordingly or choose a different meal, and tell a manager before you sit down.

### Can I park at Texas de Brazil Tampa, and is valet available?

Self-parking is available at the Boy Scout Boulevard location. I did not find valet pricing, a garage name, or a validation rule for this restaurant, so confirm those details when you call. On a stadium night or a busy weekend, leave extra time to find a space and walk in.

## Final Thoughts

Texas de Brazil Tampa is a straightforward place once you know the rules. Find the right address on Boy Scout Boulevard. Learn the token and the tongs. Go to the salad area early. Decide between weekday lunch, weekend lunch, and dinner based on price and timing. Call ahead if you have a big group or a stadium night, and do not expect a to-go box on the way out.

It is also one of several large meat-focused restaurants in the Tampa area, and the Westshore stretch is where a lot of people end up when they are headed to a game or a flight. If you go in knowing what the place is and what it is not, the evening is much easier. Pick the right door, pace yourself, and enjoy the parts that are actually included in the price.

body:
# Wright's Gourmet House Tampa: 5 Things to Know Before You Go

If you have lived in Tampa long enough, somebody has told you to go to Wright's. Usually they meant the sandwich counter on Dale Mabry, and usually they forgot to mention the hours. Wright's Gourmet House Tampa is a market-style cafe with a deli's habits, a bakery case full of cakes, and a lunch line that can wrap around the room. It is not a dinner restaurant, and that one fact clears up most of the confusion. I have been going for years, and the same mistakes keep showing up: wrong Wright's, wrong day, wrong hour, and a parking lot that is full by the time people arrive hungry. ☕ Here is what I wish someone had told me.

![Wright's Gourmet House on Dale Mabry Highway in South Tampa, front entrance at midday](https://images.pexels.com/photos/33951577/pexels-photo-33951577.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Alex Borelli](https://www.pexels.com/@alex-borelli-2155891056) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/fallingwater-in-lush-springtime-forest-33951577/)*

## Short on Time?

- **Go to Dale Mabry.** The South Tampa shop at 1200 S. Dale Mabry Highway is the Wright's most people mean. It is a deli-style restaurant for breakfast and lunch, not a dinner room.
- **It is closed Sunday and major holidays.** Weekdays run 7 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. and Saturday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Do not plan a Sunday dinner.
- **Breakfast stops at 10:30 a.m.** After that you are in sandwiches, salads, and cakes.
- **Go before 11:30 a.m. or after 1:30 p.m.** Noon is the crush. Pre-orders have their own pickup area.
- **Parking is free and it fills.** Plan for the front row to be gone at lunch. 🚗
- **The Cuban and the Martinis are the sandwiches to know.** The Cuban is pressed on request. 🥪
- **Cakes are the other reason people come back.** Slices and cupcakes work for a taste. Whole cakes need notice. 🎂
- **Catering runs on their own vans.** Do not order through a delivery app. Call 813-253-3838.

## 1. Wright's Gourmet House Tampa Is the Dale Mabry Shop, and the Other Two Are Different

The first trip-up is the name. Wright's has put several locations under one banner, and they are not interchangeable. The one people mean is the South Tampa landmark at 1200 S. Dale Mabry Highway, Tampa, FL 33629, phone 813-253-3838. That is the sandwich house, the bakery counter, and the lunch rush. It is not a steakhouse, not an Italian dining room, and not a sushi or Thai place that happens to share a city's restaurant conversation. It is a market-style cafe that still runs like a serious deli.

The other two Wright's names are easy to mix up with that shop. Tampa General Hospital has a Wright's at 1 Tampa General Circle, Tampa, FL 33606, phone 813-804-1100. It runs a different clock: seven days a week, 6 a.m. to 9 p.m., with breakfast until 10:30 a.m. That schedule is repeated right next to the Dale Mabry hours, so people blur the two. The hospital counter being open on a Sunday tells you nothing about Dale Mabry.

Then there is Wright's Market at Oxford Exchange, 420 W. Kennedy Boulevard, Tampa, FL 33606. When I checked, it was still marked "Opening Soon," even though hours were printed under that label. I would not drive to Kennedy expecting a full Wright's day until that label is gone. If someone tells you they ate at Wright's on a Sunday, they were almost certainly at the hospital, not on Dale Mabry.

This matters because a lot of people type "Wright's Gourmet House Tampa" into a map app and drive to whichever pin comes up first. Check the address before you get in the car.

![Wright's sandwich counter on Dale Mabry with the bakery case and cakes visible](https://images.pexels.com/photos/33034727/pexels-photo-33034727.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Ann H](https://www.pexels.com/@ann-h-45017) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/french-pastry-display-in-evian-les-bains-bakery-33034727/)*

## 2. Hours: Closed Sunday, Breakfast Ends at 10:30

Here is the schedule for the South Tampa shop as it is posted and repeated: Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Saturday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Closed Sunday and on major holidays. The company's answer on Sundays is a flat no. They say they have kept a weekly day off for close to 60 years, and they are not going to change that for dinner.

People still show up at 6:30 on a Friday evening or on a Sunday at all, because the word "restaurant" sounds like dinner. Dale Mabry is breakfast and lunch. Dinner is not the product. If you want a sit-down evening meal, this is not the place, and staff are not going to make an exception because you drove over from Carrollwood.

Breakfast is the other thing that trips people. The South Tampa menu I have from March 2026 stops breakfast at 10:30 a.m. The breakfast list includes the Early Riser, the Ranch Hen, the Western Scramble, The Yankee, The Sunrise, Cuban cheese toast, and quiche. If you walk in at 11 wanting eggs, you can still get a sandwich, but the morning dishes are done. The room may be open until 5:30 on a weekday. The breakfast menu is not.

Menus change, so check the day you go. The hours are the part I would not gamble on.

![Breakfast plates at the Dale Mabry counter in the morning before the 10:30 cutoff](https://images.pexels.com/photos/14415370/pexels-photo-14415370.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Connor Scott McManus](https://www.pexels.com/@connorscottmcmanus) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/hot-breakfast-on-plates-14415370/)*

## 3. The Lunch Line, the Pickup Area, and Parking

Wright's says come early, and I agree with them. The line through late morning and early afternoon is the reason most first-timers feel like they got the wrong Wright's. One customer's January 2025 visit described a kinder window: arrive before 11:30 a.m. or after 1:30 p.m. If your goal is a cake and a quiet seat, those are the times to aim for.

There is no reservation book for a table. You walk in, you order at the counter, and you take a seat in the dining room if one is free. The room seats 225, and on a busy day that is not as many seats as it sounds. If you do not find a table, you take the bag to the car and eat there. That is part of the normal routine, not a failure.

If you know what you want, pre-ordering helps. The same January 2025 visit said pre-orders pick up in a separate area, so you do not have to stand in the main line with everyone else. Ask about it when you call or when you walk in. It saves real time at noon.

Parking is the other noon problem, and it is the one I see people get most wrong. Jeff Mount, who has owned the place since 1981, answered a parking question by saying it is free and that it fills fast. A 2025 visitor described spaces in front, street parking, and a private lot with van-accessible spots. Those accounts are consistent with each other, but Wright's does not give a lot map, so I am not going to name a specific garage or lot. Dale Mabry at lunch is not a side street where you can park on a whim. If the front row is taken, circling for a spot is how a lunch break dies.

My practical advice: arrive before 11:30 or after 1:30, park wherever you find a space without fuss, and leave the pickup window for someone who has a ticket in hand.

![Line of customers at the Dale Mabry counter during the lunch rush with the deli case in view](https://images.pexels.com/photos/31539254/pexels-photo-31539254.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Maksim Romashkin](https://www.pexels.com/@maksim-romashkin) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/fast-food-restaurant-staff-at-counter-in-oslo-31539254/)*

## 4. What to Order: The Cuban, the Martinis, and Bucket Bread

The menu is long, but the sandwiches are the reason to come, and the bread matters more than most people expect. Most of the sandwiches are built on Bucket Bread. The story is that a German baker's round-pan dough became the house bread, and it is still the one you will see on almost every sandwich. Other breads on the menu include pumpernickel, rye, whole wheat, Cuban bread, and onion rolls.

The Cuban is the one I would order first. On the March 2026 menu it was $14, with roasted pork, ham, Genoa salami, pickles, Jarlsberg, and mustard on Cuban bread. It has won a local paper's best-Cuban contest six times, and it is pressed on request, so ask for it hot if you like it that way. Prices change, so treat that number as the March figure, not a promise.

The Golden Gate is older than that contest, and it is the one I think of when someone asks what the place is really about. It is pork and bacon with a German dill pickle, Pete's Mustard Sauce, and peach chutney on pumpernickel. The sweet-and-tart combination is not something you find on every deli menu in town.

Then there are the Martinis. The Beef Martini has rare roast beef, white-wine mushrooms, bacon, and garlic-herb butter. It was created in 1976, and the company still bills it as imitated and never duplicated. The Turkey Martini is the turkey version of the same idea. If you are indecisive, the staff will tell you that turkey breast on pumpernickel is the most popular sandwich. Paris is turkey, brie, and apple, and it is a good pick if you want something a little sweeter.

The salads are where the people who cannot choose one sandwich end up. You can get them by the scoop: turkey and pecan (the most popular salad, the counter staff will tell you), pesto pasta, shrimp pasta, broccoli and peanut, Greek potato, tuna, and chicken salad. The soups are made from scratch and rotate with a feature. Some plates, like the Turkey and Pecan Salad Plate, come with no substitutions. Groups try to rebuild those plates at the counter, and it usually ends with someone frustrated. Order what is on the plate or pick a different one.

Garden salads can drop the croutons if you ask. Most deli salads are gluten-free, but the bread and desserts are not, which I come back to below.

![Cuban sandwich on Cuban bread with pickles and mustard on a Wright's wrapper](https://images.pexels.com/photos/32480062/pexels-photo-32480062.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Vladimir Srajber](https://www.pexels.com/@vladimirsrajber) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/delicious-cheeseburger-with-pickles-on-a-plate-32480062/)*

## 5. Cakes and Catering

The cakes are the part people remember years later, and they were not on the original 1963 menu. The shop started as a gourmet market where you could buy delicacies, coffees, cheeses, roasted meats, and big wheel sandwiches. Over time the bakery became the other half of the reputation. The company calls some of its recipes sacred, including a rum cake that a regular originally insisted be sold only here.

The March 2026 cake list included Alpine, carrot, coconut, hummingbird, chocolate, red velvet, peanut butter chocolate, Hawaiian Princess, strawberry, and peppermint chocolate. Hummingbird is the birthday cake people order most. Peppermint chocolate and chocolate rum cake were listed only for November and December, so it is October as I write this, and you should ask before you plan around them. Another customer's 2025 account said the coconut cream pie was gone, so I am not promising a pie. Ask what is in the case the day you go.

For a whole cake, plan on a message and at least a day's notice. For a taste, slices and cupcakes do the job. There is no separate tasting appointment, and you do not need one. Just ask at the counter.

Catering is where things get stuck most often. Wright's does not use Uber Eats, Grubhub, or similar apps for its orders. The company runs its own refrigerated vans for inside delivery. If you see the name on a delivery app, I would not trust that order. Call 813-253-3838 and ask for catering directly.

Delivery is mainly for large orders and runs inside a half-hour window. The primary area is the Tampa city limits, with adjoining areas possible. Fees depend on zone, time of day, and order size. The peak windows on the menu are 7 to 9 a.m., 11 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., and 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. Off-peak is what they suggest for cakes. Slots fill several days out, and in the holiday season three to four weeks out. You can hold a time and send the food later if your schedule shifts.

Orders of $500 or more need a 50 percent deposit and 48 hours' notice to cancel. Holiday baking requests need at least four weeks, because the oven is full during that stretch, and off-menu custom requests get turned down. I would not plan a holiday office lunch around a last-minute yes.

There is a meeting space that holds up to 80 people in one room, but you have to ask for it. It is not something you wander into from the lunch line. "Bag and Tag" means each person's order goes in a labeled bag, which is useful for office lunches. Volume breaks often hit at 12 and 25 count. They will not do half sandwiches, though they will cut a whole one. There is no combo meal and no senior, military, or student discount that I have heard of. They accept cash, American Express, Discover, Mastercard, Visa, and gift cards. They have shipped Cubans overnight, but the owner's own warnings apply: bread softens once it is wrapped, and dry-ice shipping costs real money. If shipping is really the plan, call the catering line and choose the option for it. There are no Wright's T-shirts.

![Catering trays and Bag and Tag sandwiches in a Wright's delivery van at the back of the South Tampa shop](https://images.pexels.com/photos/33419116/pexels-photo-33419116.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Mad Knoxx Deluxe](https://www.pexels.com/@madknoxxdeluxe) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/appetizing-mini-sandwiches-on-display-33419116/)*

## Useful Things to Know

**Confirm the location before you leave the house.** Dale Mabry is the sandwich shop. The hospital counter is a separate phone number and a separate clock. Oxford Exchange was still marked "Opening Soon" when I checked, with hours sitting under that warning. Treat that as a trap until the label disappears.

**Do not plan a Sunday.** The South Tampa shop is closed on Sundays and major holidays. The hospital is open seven days, so if you need a weekend Wright's fix, that is the one to aim for, but it is a different experience.

**Breakfast ends at 10:30 on weekdays.** On the March 2026 menu the cutoff was 10:30 a.m. If you want the egg dishes, be there early.

**Lunch has a rhythm.** The worst stretch I have seen runs from late morning to about 1:30. The easier windows are before 11:30 and after 1:30. Pre-order and use the separate pickup if you can.

**Parking is free, but it fills.** The front spaces, street parking, and a private lot have all been described to me. The front row goes first. Give yourself a few extra minutes for the search, or go during the easier windows.

**Allergens are everywhere.** Milk, eggs, tree nuts, peanuts, shellfish, and wheat show up across the building, and the company will not guarantee a free-from item. Most deli salads are gluten-free, but there is no gluten-free bread and no gluten-free dessert. A Bucket Bread sandwich is the wrong order for someone who needs to avoid gluten. The company does not publish nutrition numbers, so ask if you need them.

**Catering is a phone call.** Do not put a catering order through a delivery app. Call 813-253-3838. Orders of $500 or more need a deposit. Holidays need weeks of notice, not hours.

**Wright's is not a steakhouse, an Italian restaurant, or a sushi or Thai place.** People who expect a dinner restaurant leave disappointed. Think sandwiches, salads, soups, cakes, and a counter.

## FAQ

### Is Wright's Gourmet House Tampa open on Sundays?

Not the South Tampa shop on Dale Mabry. It is closed Sunday and on major holidays, and the company has kept that weekly day off for close to 60 years. The Tampa General Hospital counter is open seven days a week, from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m., but that is a different location.

### What time does Wright's Gourmet House Tampa close on weekdays?

On Dale Mabry, weekday hours run from 7 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., and Saturday runs 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Breakfast stops at 10:30 a.m. on the South Tampa menu, so the egg dishes are only in the morning.

### What is the best time to go to avoid the lunch line?

Before 11:30 a.m. or after 1:30 p.m. The noon window is the busiest. If you pre-order, use the separate pickup area so you are not standing in the main line.

### Is parking free at the Dale Mabry location?

Jeff Mount, who has owned the business since 1981, says parking is free and fills fast. Visitors have described front spaces, street parking, and a private lot with van-accessible spots. Wright's does not publish a lot map, so plan to look for a space when you arrive, and go during the easier windows if you can.

### What should I order at Wright's Gourmet House Tampa?

Start with the Cuban, which was $14 on the March 2026 menu and is pressed on request. The Golden Gate and the Beef Martini are the other two I would try. Pick turkey and pecan salad if you want a scoop, and get a slice or a cupcake for dessert. Prices change, so check the current menu when you order.

### Can I order Wright's catering through Uber Eats or Grubhub?

No. Wright's runs its own refrigerated vans for inside delivery and does not use delivery apps for catering. Call 813-253-3838 to place a catering order. Orders of $500 or more need a 50 percent deposit and 48 hours' notice to cancel.

### Does Wright's have gluten-free options?

Most deli salads are gluten-free, and garden salads can be made without croutons. There is no gluten-free bread and no gluten-free dessert, and most sandwiches are built on Bucket Bread. The company will not guarantee that any item is free from allergens, so people with serious allergies should ask before ordering.

### Do I need a reservation for a table?

No. There is no reservation book for a table. You order at the counter and take a seat if one is free. The dining room seats 225, but on a busy lunch you may end up taking your food to the car.

## Final Thoughts

Wright's Gourmet House Tampa is one of those places that rewards you for knowing what it is. Go to the Dale Mabry shop for breakfast or lunch, plan around the Sunday closure, and get there before the noon rush if you can. Order a Cuban, try a Martini, and bring something home from the cake case. If you are planning a party or an office lunch, call the catering line early and skip the delivery apps. The room on Dale Mabry is the one worth the trip. It is a counter that expects you at lunch, not at candlelight, and that is exactly why people keep coming back.

title: Tampa to Naples: 4 Things to Know Before You Drive
dek: Tampa to Naples is 164 miles on the state chart, Naples to Tampa is 162. Here's the I-75 route, the exits that matter, and how to avoid Alligator Alley.

body:
# Tampa to Naples: 4 Things to Know Before You Drive

If you are searching for tampa to naples directions, the first thing to know is that the trip doesn't come with one number. People ask it every way you can imagine: tampa to naples, naples to tampa, tampa fl to naples fl, naples fl to tampa fl. Those all mean the same road, but the mileage, the exits, and the toll question shift depending on which way you're going and which city you're trying to reach. I have made this drive enough times to know where people get tripped up. 🚗

![Interstate 75 heading south through the Tampa Bay area toward Naples at midday](https://images.pexels.com/photos/13976369/pexels-photo-13976369.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [John Hill](https://www.pexels.com/@john-hill-822587) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/aerial-view-of-highway-interchange-13976369/)*

## Short on Time?

- Tampa to Naples is 164 miles on the state's official highway mileage chart. Naples to Tampa is 162. I keep both numbers.
- The route is I-75 south. It stays toll-free north of exit 101 near Naples.
- Alligator Alley is a different toll road. It runs east toward Miami, and you only touch it if you go that way.
- Florida's exit numbers count up from the Miami end, not from Tampa. Don't do math on mileposts to estimate the drive.
- I don't have a drive time I trust, so I'm not giving one. Check tolls and conditions before you leave.

## 1. Tampa to Naples: The Official Miles Both Ways

Let's start with the number, since it's the question I get most. The state publishes an official highway mileage chart that lists the shortest distance between city pairs in Florida. The version I went by was updated September 14, 2026. On that chart, Tampa to Naples is 164 miles. Naples to Tampa is 162 miles.

If you searched for tampa to naples fl or tampa fl to naples fl, you're asking about that same pair. The direction still matters, though.

Those two numbers don't match, and I'm not going to smooth them into one. You could call it 163, or "about 160," and it would look tidier. But that would be me making up a number. The chart doesn't explain why the two directions differ, and I'm not going to invent a reason. If you need a figure for a form, use the one that matches your direction of travel.

The same chart has other pairs that people often lump together, and I try to keep them separate. Tampa to Fort Myers is 124 miles, and Fort Myers to Tampa is 125. Fort Myers to Naples is 37 miles in either direction. You can't add 124 and 37 to get a Tampa-to-Naples trip through Fort Myers, and comparing that sum to 164 doesn't tell you anything useful. Fort Myers is its own pair.

Other pairs on the chart work the same way. Tampa to Sarasota is 52 miles both ways. Sarasota to Naples is 113, and Naples to Sarasota is 114. Tampa to Bradenton is 41, and Bradenton to Tampa is 40. Tampa to Punta Gorda is 103 both ways. Naples to Miami is 109 both ways, but Miami is a different trip. It's the east-west crossing through the Everglades, not a stop on the gulf drive.

So if someone asks you how far it is, the honest answer is "164 going south, 162 coming back, both on I-75." That's a clean answer, and it's accurate.

![Highway distance sign along I-75 in Southwest Florida showing miles to Naples](https://images.pexels.com/photos/37774954/pexels-photo-37774954.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Matheus Bertelli](https://www.pexels.com/@bertellifotografia) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/key-west-directional-road-sign-on-sunny-day-37774954/)*

## 2. The Interstate You Actually Drive

Most of this trip is I-75. In Florida, the whole interstate is a little under 471 miles, so the number you see on a sign or a map for the full state is not the Tampa-to-Naples distance. People see "471" and think it applies to their drive. It doesn't. It's the whole state.

The speed limit is 70 mph on I-75 throughout Florida. I'm not going to turn the 164 miles into a travel time by dividing by 70. The city pair isn't a promise that every mile gets driven at the limit, and it isn't measured exit to exit. Traffic, construction, and merges all change the real time, and I don't have a number I'd stand behind.

Here's the rough shape of the route. Heading south from Tampa, I-75 stays on the east side of the bay. You pass through Brandon, then Temple Terrace, then New Tampa. Keep going, and the interstate runs past Bonita Springs, Fort Myers, Punta Gorda, Port Charlotte, Venice, Sarasota, and Bradenton before you get into the Naples end.

Two things can throw you off on the Tampa side. First, I-75 doesn't take you downtown. It passes the city. If you want downtown, you have to leave the interstate on purpose, either on the Lee Roy Selmon Expressway (SR 618) or on I-4, which also heads toward Orlando. Second, if you're going to St. Petersburg, you leave I-75 for I-275. North of Ellenton, I-275 splits off toward St. Petersburg over the Sunshine Skyway and toward Tampa over the Howard Frankland. That's a different destination than Naples, and it gets people headed the wrong way if they're not paying attention.

Going north from Naples, you'll see Sarasota and Bradenton before the Tampa Bay area. The route is simple once you know it's one highway. The confusion mostly comes from the names of the exits and the cities, which we'll get to next.

![Interstate 75 near Wesley Chapel with overpass and southbound traffic at dusk](https://images.pexels.com/photos/20021120/pexels-photo-20021120.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Thomas  balabaud](https://www.pexels.com/@thomas-balabaud-735585) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/cars-on-highway-20021120/)*

## 3. The Exits Count From Miami, Not Tampa

This is the trap I want you to avoid. Florida numbers its exits starting from the Miami end of I-75. So the numbers go up as you move north and west toward Tampa, not down. If you're driving south from Tampa, the exit numbers get smaller as you go. If you're counting from Tampa, you'll get confused fast.

For the Naples end, here are the exits that matter, roughly in order as you approach. Exit 101 is CR 951, toward Naples and Marco Island, and it's where Alligator Alley ends. Exit 105 is Golden Gate Parkway toward Naples. Exit 111 is Immokalee Road. Exit 116 is Bonita Beach Road. Exit 123 is Corkscrew Road in Estero. Exit 128 is Alico Road, toward Southwest Florida International Airport. Exit 131 is Daniels Parkway, and there's a rest area northeast of that interchange. Exit 136 is Colonial Boulevard in Fort Myers. Exit 141 is SR 80, Palm Beach Boulevard. After that comes the Caloosahatchee bridge, and then SR 78 at exit 143 for North Fort Myers and Cape Coral.

Now the Tampa end, from the other direction. Punta Gorda is around exits 161 and 164. There's a weigh station near mile 158.8. University Parkway at exit 213 is the route to the Sarasota-Bradenton airport. I-275 north toward St. Petersburg is at exit 228. There's a rest area near Ruskin at mile 237.2. The Selmon is at exit 256 in Brandon, toward Tampa and the port. I-4 is at exit 261, toward Tampa and Orlando. And I-275 south is at exit 274 in Wesley Chapel, toward Tampa, St. Petersburg, and the airport.

Here's why this matters. If you take exit 105 and exit 261 and subtract one from the other, you'll get a number, and it won't be the drive. Those mileposts start near Miami Lakes. Golden Gate Parkway isn't the city point for Naples, and the I-4 interchange isn't the city point for Tampa. The official pairs are 164 one way and 162 the other. The exits are landmarks, not a calculator.

What the exits are good for is recognizing where you are. When you see Wesley Chapel, you know you're on the north side of the trip. When you see Colonial Boulevard in Fort Myers, you know you're getting close to the bottom half. That's the use I get from them.

The rest areas on I-75 are the other thing to plan around. I stop at them more than I expected to. The ones I've used have restrooms, vending, picnic tables, dog walks, and nighttime security. I haven't inventoried gas or food beyond that, so plan your own fuel stops.

![Exit sign for Golden Gate Parkway on I-75 near Naples with palm trees along the road](https://images.pexels.com/photos/12908882/pexels-photo-12908882.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Robert So](https://www.pexels.com/@robertkso) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/highway-in-city-12908882/)*

## 4. Alligator Alley Is the Other Direction

This is the mix-up I kept running into. People hear "Naples" and "toll" in the same breath and assume the whole drive is a toll road. It isn't.

Alligator Alley, also called Everglades Parkway, is the tolled east-west part of I-75. It runs from exit 19 in Sunrise, near Fort Lauderdale, to exit 101 just east of Naples. That's about 75 miles of toll road, overseen by Florida's Turnpike Enterprise. It passes through the Big Cypress National Preserve and runs past the Florida Panther National Wildlife Refuge, so expect long stretches with not much around you. At exit 101, the alley ends. The road turns north, and the Interstate is toll-free for the rest of its length in Florida. Tampa, Fort Myers, Sarasota, and Bradenton all sit on that toll-free side.

So unless you drive past Naples and keep going east toward Miami or Fort Lauderdale, you won't touch Alligator Alley. The toll is not part of a Tampa-to-Naples drive. The one way to end up on it by accident is to miss the bend at exit 101 and head east when you wanted to go north or stay on the Naples side. That's a real mistake, and I've seen people make it at the Naples end. 🐊

The toll details are where I have to be careful. The last rate I have is $3.75 for a two-axle vehicle, which was in effect as of July 1, 2023, payable by cash or SunPass at the plazas. I don't have a current rate card I trust, so don't treat that figure as today's price. I also heard that Alligator Alley stopped taking cash on August 3, 2026, and went all-electronic. I haven't confirmed that, so check before you rely on it, especially if you're planning to pay at a plaza with cash.

There's a bit of history that explains why people expect a toll on the gulf side anyway. In the 1960s, Florida proposed a West Coast Turnpike from the Tampa Bay area south to Naples. That tolled turnpike was canceled in 1968, when the I-75 extension south to Naples and then east to Miami was approved instead. The Tampa-to-Naples interstate was complete by 1986, and the extension was built as an interstate, not as that turnpike. I'm mentioning this because the old plan is probably why the toll question keeps coming up. It's not a reason to expect a toll on the trip you're taking now.

Naples to Miami is 109 miles on the chart. That's its own trip, and it is the one that puts you on Alligator Alley. If Miami is where you're headed, plan it as a separate drive.

![Alligator Alley toll plaza on I-75 east of Naples with the Everglades flat and open on both sides](https://images.pexels.com/photos/19924365/pexels-photo-19924365.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&dpr=2&h=650&w=940)
*Photo by [Alain Garcia](https://www.pexels.com/@shotbyadrone) on [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/crocodile-on-a-swamp-19924365/)*

## Useful Things to Know

Here are the practical points I'd want to know before the drive.

Plan the Naples end carefully. Exit 101 is where the toll road meets the toll-free interstate, so pay attention to signs there. Exit 105 for Golden Gate Parkway is on the toll-free north-south road. If you want to get off near Naples, make sure you're on the right side of the bend before you commit.

Know what I-75 won't do for you. It won't drop you in downtown Tampa, and it won't take you to St. Petersburg unless you leave for I-275. If you're going to a specific part of Tampa, look at which expressway gets you closest before you're near the city. The Selmon Expressway and I-4 are both options from I-75, but I never got a Selmon toll rate, so I'm not going to put a price on that exit.

Keep the two directions straight. If you're writing down the distance, put 164 next to "Tampa to Naples" and 162 next to "Naples to Tampa." Don't average them. If you're giving directions to someone, tell them which way you're going, because the two numbers aren't the same.

Don't turn exits into math. People try to figure out the trip length from the exit numbers, and it doesn't work. The numbers start at Miami, and the milepost for the city point isn't the same as the exit you use to get there. Use the exits to recognize places as you go by.

Watch the weigh station and rest areas. There's a weigh station near mile 158.8, and rest areas at mile 237.2 near Ruskin and near exit 131 in Daniels Parkway. Plan your stops with those in mind, and check current conditions on the road, since things change.

Don't assume the toll is the same as it was. The Alligator Alley toll details I have are dated, and I heard about a payment change in August 2026 that I haven't confirmed. Check the current rules before you go, especially if you plan to use cash.

Give yourself room for traffic in the Tampa area. The Selmon and I-4 junctions are where you'll make decisions, and I don't have a drive time I trust, so pad your estimate instead of relying on a formula.

## FAQ

### How many miles is tampa to naples?

The state's official highway mileage chart lists Tampa to Naples as 164 miles. Naples to Tampa is listed as 162 miles. I keep both numbers because they differ, and I don't average them or invent a reason for the gap.

### Why is naples to tampa a different number than tampa to naples?

The chart gives different figures for each direction, and it doesn't explain why. I'm not going to guess. If you need one number for a specific purpose, use the figure that matches the direction you're traveling.

### Is there a toll on the drive from tampa fl to naples fl?

Not on the I-75 route from Tampa to Naples. The toll road is Alligator Alley, which runs east from exit 101 near Naples toward Miami. You only touch it if you go past Naples heading east. I don't have a current toll rate I trust, so check before you go.

### Which exit do I take to get to Naples?

It depends on where you're going in Naples. Exit 101 is CR 951 toward Naples and Marco Island, and it's where Alligator Alley ends. Exit 105 is Golden Gate Parkway toward Naples. Choose based on your destination, and pay attention at the bend near exit 101 so you don't head onto the toll road by accident.

### How long does the naples fl to tampa fl drive take?

I don't have a drive time I trust, so I'm not going to give one. The state's speed limit on I-75 is 70 mph throughout Florida, but the real time depends on traffic, construction, and where you start and finish. Plan extra time, especially through the Tampa area.

### Do I have to go through Fort Myers on the way from Tampa to Naples?

I-75 passes right by Fort Myers on the way, and the route goes through several exits connected to the city, including Colonial Boulevard at exit 136. Fort Myers is its own pair on the mileage chart, though. Don't add the Tampa-Fort Myers and Fort Myers-Naples numbers together to get a trip distance.

### Where does I-75 drop me off in downtown Tampa?

It doesn't. I-75 passes east of the bay through Brandon, Temple Terrace, and New Tampa. To reach downtown, you leave on the Lee Roy Selmon Expressway (SR 618) or on I-4, which heads toward Orlando. St. Petersburg is reached by leaving for I-275 instead.

### Is the Tampa to Naples drive the same as the Alligator Alley drive?

No. The Tampa-to-Naples trip is on I-75, and the stretch north of exit 101 near Naples is toll-free. Alligator Alley is the tolled east-west piece that runs from near Sunrise to exit 101. It's a separate trip, and you only use it if you're heading to Miami or Fort Lauderdale from Naples.

## Final Thoughts

The short version is simple. Tampa to Naples is I-75 south, 164 miles on the state chart going south and 162 coming back. The toll road people worry about is a different trip, and you only meet it if you keep going east past Naples. The exit numbers start at Miami, so they're landmarks, not a way to measure the drive.

I'd take the interstate, keep the two directions written down separately, and check the current toll rules before you go. Those three things will save you most of the confusion I've seen people run into. Safe driving, and enjoy the drive south. 🛣️
